questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon SageMaker to deploy a model that determines whether social media posts contain specific topics. The company must demonstrate how different input features affect the model's behavior. Which SageMaker feature satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Clarify provides model explainability through feature attribution, showing how individual input features contribute to model predictions. It also supports NLP explainability for text features.
learnMore: Model Explainability - Amazon SageMaker AI
ClarifyTextConfig - Amazon SageMaker API Reference

questions.questionText: Which option describes a characteristic of transformer-based language models?
options: A. Transformer-based language models use convolutional layers to apply filters across an input to capture local patterns through filtered views.
B. Transformer-based language models can process only text data.
C. Transformer-based language models use self-attention mechanisms to capture contextual relationships.
D. Transformer-based language models process data sequences one element at a time in cyclic iterations.
questions.explanation: Transformer-based language models use self-attention to model contextual relationships among tokens in an input sequence. This enables each token representation to incorporate relevant information from other tokens.
learnMore: What are Transformers? (AWS)

questions.questionText: A company wants to build an ML application.
questions.explanation: The ML lifecycle starts by identifying the business outcome and framing it as an ML problem. The model is then built, trained, tuned, and evaluated; the validated model is deployed to production; and its production performance is monitored for degradation or drift.
learnMore: Well-Architected machine learning lifecycle - Machine Learning Lens

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: An AI practitioner trained a custom model on Amazon Bedrock by using a training dataset that contains confidential data. The AI practitioner wants to ensure that the custom model does not generate inference responses based on confidential data. How should the AI practitioner prevent responses based on confidential data?
options: A. Delete the custom model. Remove the confidential data from the training dataset. Retrain the custom model.
B. Mask the confidential data in the inference responses by using dynamic data masking.
C. Encrypt the confidential data in the inference responses by using Amazon SageMaker.
D. Encrypt the confidential data in the custom model by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
questions.explanation: Once a model is trained, confidential data becomes embedded in the model's parameters. The only way to ensure the model does not generate responses based on confidential information is to delete the model, remove sensitive data from the training dataset, and retrain from scratch.
learnMore: Delete a custom model (Amazon Bedrock)
Data protection (Amazon Bedrock)

questions.questionText: A publishing company has built a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)-based solution that lets users interact with published content. New content is published each day. The company wants to deliver a near-real-time user experience. Which steps of the RAG pipeline should the company perform using offline batch processing to meet these requirements? Choose two
options: B. Generation of embeddings for user queries
C. Creation of the search index
E. Response generation for the user
questions.explanation: Content embeddings and the search index are produced during the data-ingestion phase, before user requests arrive. Batch processing these steps keeps newly published content available for subsequent low-latency query embedding, retrieval, and response generation. AWS guidance describes document embedding and vector-database ingestion as the upfront RAG step, followed by query submission, retrieval, and LLM response generation.
learnMore: Understanding Retrieval Augmented Generation

questions.questionText: A company needs to assess AI-generated summaries against reference text. It must measure semantic similarity and coverage of key information. Which metrics satisfy these requirements? Choose two
options: E. Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE)
questions.explanation: BERTScore measures similarity between generated and reference text using contextual BERT embeddings, enabling semantic comparisons. ROUGE measures overlap with the reference and is recall-oriented, making it suitable for assessing whether a summary covers key reference information.
learnMore: Review metrics for an automated model evaluation job in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company has trained a foundation model (FM) for a specific task. The company must fine-tune the FM to carry out a different but related task. Which fine-tuning method meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: Transfer learning adapts a pretrained model to a new, related task by continuing training with task-specific data, reusing the model’s previously learned representations. AWS documentation identifies fine-tuning of a pretrained model on a new dataset as transfer learning.
learnMore: Fine-Tune a Model - Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: A company has built a chatbot that can respond to natural language questions with images. The company wants to ensure that the chatbot does not return inappropriate or unwanted images. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: B. Retrain the model with a general public dataset.
questions.explanation: Moderation APIs are specifically designed to scan generated content before delivery and filter or block inappropriate material such as explicit or harmful images. They integrate directly into chatbot workflows to prevent harmful outputs. Retraining with public data, model validation alone, and user feedback integration do not provide real-time content filtering capabilities.
learnMore: Block harmful images with content filters – Amazon Bedrock
Detect and filter harmful content using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company wants to use a large language model (LLM) to develop a conversational agent. The company needs to prevent the LLM from being manipulated with common prompt engineering techniques to perform undesirable actions or expose sensitive information. Which action will reduce these risks?
options: A. Create a prompt template that teaches the LLM to detect attack patterns.
B. Increase the temperature parameter on invocation requests to the LLM.
C. Avoid using LLMs that are not listed in Amazon SageMaker.
D. Decrease the number of input tokens on invocations of the LLM.
questions.explanation: Creating a prompt template that instructs the LLM to recognize and resist common attack patterns (prompt injection, malicious requests) strengthens the model's ability to defend itself against manipulation. By explicitly teaching the model its boundaries and expected behaviors, you reduce the risk of undesirable outputs and data exposure. Increasing temperature amplifies randomness (counterproductive), restricting to specific platforms lacks security benefit, and limiting input tokens risks losing critical context.
learnMore: Prompt injection security – Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company regularly refreshes its product database by manually uploading digital product guides. The guides include text and images. The company wants to automate this work with generative AI.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 provides the object storage location for the digital guides. Amazon Nova multimodal models can analyze both text and image inputs, allowing the product data to be extracted or structured after the files are available. That processed output can then be used to insert records into the product database.

questions.questionText: Sentiment analysis belongs to which broader AI field?
questions.explanation: Sentiment analysis extracts or classifies opinions, attitudes, and emotional tone from human language, making it a natural language processing (NLP) application.
learnMore: What is Amazon Comprehend?
Sentiment analysis (Amazon Comprehend)

questions.questionText: Which option characterizes embeddings in the context of AI?
options: A. A method for compressing large datasets
B. An encryption method for securing sensitive data
C. A method for visualizing high-dimensional data
D. A numerical method for data representation in a reduced dimensionality space
questions.explanation: Embeddings encode items as numerical vectors in a reduced-dimensional space, allowing models to represent and compare semantic or structural relationships mathematically.
learnMore: What is Embedding? (AWS)

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company is developing a conversational AI assistant. The company intends to use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to stop users from trying to bypass the AI assistant’s built-in safety capabilities. Which type of Bedrock Guardrail policy meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: The prompt attacks policy detects and filters jailbreaks and prompt-injection attempts intended to override developer instructions or bypass a foundation model’s built-in safety and moderation capabilities.
learnMore: Detect prompt attacks with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

questions.questionText: Which functionality does Amazon SageMaker Clarify provide?
options: A. Integrates a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) workflow
B. Monitors the quality of ML models in production
C. Documents critical details about ML models
D. Identifies potential bias during data preparation
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Clarify's primary functionality is identifying potential bias in datasets during data preparation, helping practitioners detect imbalances and fairness issues before model training. This early detection is crucial for building responsible and fair ML systems. RAG workflows are for retrieval-augmented generation (a different task), Model Monitor (not Clarify) monitors production performance, and model documentation is a different function.
learnMore: Pre-training Bias Metrics – Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: A media-streaming platform wants to deliver movie recommendations to users based on their account history. Which AWS service fulfills these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize generates personalized recommendations from users’ item-interaction history. Its User-Personalization-v2 recipe is specifically suited to personalized movie recommendations for a streaming application.
learnMore: User-Personalization-v2 recipe — Amazon Personalize

questions.questionText: A company intends to add generative AI capabilities to its application by integrating a large language model (LLM). The LLM responses must be as deterministic and stable as possible. Which solution fulfills these requirements?
options: A. Configure the application to automatically set the temperature parameter to 0 when submitting the prompt to the LLM.
B. Configure the application to automatically add "make your response deterministic" at the end of the prompt before submitting the prompt to the LLM.
C. Configure the application to automatically add "make your response deterministic" at the beginning of the prompt before submitting the prompt to the LLM.
D. Configure the application to automatically set the temperature parameter to 1 when submitting the prompt to the LLM.
questions.explanation: Temperature is the inference parameter that controls response randomness. A temperature of 0 minimizes randomness and therefore yields the most deterministic and stable output for the same prompt; instructing the model in prompt text does not provide the same sampling control, while a temperature of 1 increases variation.
learnMore: Design a prompt - Amazon Bedrock

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A financial institution is using Amazon Bedrock to develop an AI application. The application is hosted in a VPC. To meet regulatory compliance standards, the VPC is not allowed access to any internet traffic. Which AWS service or feature will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS PrivateLink enables private, secure connectivity between VPCs and AWS services without exposing traffic to the public internet. This satisfies regulatory compliance requirements that prohibit internet access while allowing the VPC to access Bedrock and other AWS services over AWS's internal network. Macie provides data security, CloudFront distributes content, and an Internet Gateway provides public internet access—none solve the compliance constraint.
learnMore: Use AWS PrivateLink with Amazon Bedrock
Protect your data using Amazon VPC and AWS PrivateLink

questions.questionText: A company is introducing a mobile app that helps users learn foreign languages. The app makes text more coherent by calling a large language model (LLM). The company collected a diverse dataset of text and supplemented the dataset with examples of more readable versions. The company wants the LLM output to resemble the provided examples. Which metric should the company use to assess whether the LLM meets these requirements?
options: A. Value of the loss function
C. Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE) score
D. Latency of the text generation
questions.explanation: ROUGE (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation) is specifically designed to measure how well generated text matches reference examples by calculating n-gram overlap, precision, recall, and F1 scores. Since the company has reference examples of readable text and wants the model's output to resemble them, ROUGE directly evaluates this alignment. The loss function measures training performance, semantic robustness measures resilience, and latency measures speed—none assess output similarity to examples.
learnMore: Use metrics to understand model performance (Amazon Bedrock)

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner is creating a prompt for large language models (LLMs) in Amazon Bedrock. The practitioner must ensure that the prompt works across all Amazon Bedrock LLMs. Which characteristic may vary among the LLMs?
options: C. The ability to control model output randomness
D. Compatibility with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock models can have different maximum generated-response token limits. A prompt and its requested output length must therefore remain within the maximum token count supported by every target model. AWS notes that inference-parameter defaults and valid ranges depend on the model, and maxTokens defaults to the maximum permitted by the selected model.
learnMore: Influence response generation with inference parameters - Amazon Bedrock
InferenceConfiguration - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company is building a chatbot that uses Amazon Lex and Amazon OpenSearch Service. The chatbot uses the company’s private data to answer questions. The company must convert the data into a vector representation before storing it in a database. Which type of foundation model (FM) meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: A text embeddings model converts text into numerical vector representations that capture semantic meaning. Those embeddings can be stored in Amazon OpenSearch Service for vector similarity search and retrieval of relevant private data. Amazon Titan Text Embeddings models
learnMore: Vector search in Amazon OpenSearch Service

questions.questionText: A company wants to build a generative AI application by using Amazon Bedrock and needs to choose a foundation model (FM). The company wants to know how much information can fit into one prompt. Which consideration will inform the company's decision?
questions.explanation: The context window defines the maximum number of tokens (input and output combined) a foundation model can process in a single prompt. This directly determines how much information can fit into one prompt. Temperature controls output randomness, batch size relates to throughput efficiency, and model size refers to parameter count—none of these affect individual prompt length limits.
learnMore: Models at a glance - Amazon Bedrock
Supported foundation models in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company plans to develop ML applications to improve business operations and efficiency.
questions.explanation: Binary and multi-class classification predict labeled class values and therefore use supervised learning. K-means clustering groups unlabeled observations, and dimensionality reduction generally discovers a lower-dimensional representation without labels; both are unsupervised learning.
learnMore: Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning
K-Means Algorithm - Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: A company is using a pre-trained large language model (LLM) to build a chatbot for product recommendations. The company needs the LLM outputs to be short and written in a specific language. Which solution will align the LLM response quality with the company's expectations?
options: B. Choose an LLM of a different size.
D. Increase the Top K value.
questions.explanation: Adjusting the prompt allows direct control over LLM output characteristics including length and language. By crafting instructions like 'Respond in [language] with 2-3 sentences', the model aligns with requirements. Model size, temperature, and top-K control different aspects of generation (creativity, diversity) but do not directly constrain output length or language.
learnMore: Prompt engineering concepts - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company uses a foundation model (FM) to generate creative marketing slogans for a range of products. The company wants to reuse a standard template containing common instructions when creating slogans for different products. However, it must add a short description for each product. Which Amazon Bedrock solution meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Prompt management lets organizations create and save reusable prompt templates with shared instructions. Variables in the template can be populated at invocation time with each product’s short description, while retaining the common slogan-generation instructions.
learnMore: Construct and store reusable prompts with Prompt management in Amazon Bedrock
Create a prompt using Prompt management

questions.questionText: A company is developing a generative AI application on AWS. The application will help students improve their reading comprehension. It must enable students to add illustrations to stories. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Use Amazon Bedrock Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large to generate images based on text inputs.
B. Use Amazon Polly to create an audiobook based on story texts.
C. Use Amazon Rekognition to analyze image contents and detect text attributes.
D. Create a standard prompt template. Use Amazon Q Business to illustrate stories.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Stability.ai Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large supports text-to-image generation from a text prompt, enabling illustrations to be generated for story content. AWS documentation: Stability.ai Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large
learnMore: Stability.ai Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: Which technique can a company use to lower bias and toxicity in generative AI applications during the post-processing ML lifecycle?
questions.explanation: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) is a post-processing technique where human reviewers evaluate and filter generated outputs to identify and remove biased or toxic content before delivery to end-users. This directly addresses the requirement to reduce bias and toxicity in the post-processing phase. Data augmentation and feature engineering are training-phase techniques, while adversarial training improves model robustness but does not directly filter outputs for toxicity.

questions.questionText: A company wants to improve employee productivity by using a generative AI solution to write code for testing software applications. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
questions.explanation: Amazon Q Developer is a managed generative AI assistant for software development that can generate code and unit tests in supported IDEs. It directly supports automated test-code generation without the custom agent implementation required by Amazon Bedrock Agents.
learnMore: Chatting with Amazon Q Developer about code

questions.questionText: A company needs to choose a generative AI model to build an application. The application must return responses to users in real time. Which model characteristic should the company evaluate to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Inference speed determines how quickly a generative AI model produces responses after receiving user input, making it the relevant characteristic for real-time interactions.
learnMore: Optimize model inference for latency - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company is developing a generative AI tool. The company will use internal documents to customize a foundation model (FM). Which approach meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: Continued pre-training trains a foundation model further on an organization’s unlabeled documents, expanding its domain knowledge and customizing it for that organization’s content. Amazon Bedrock identifies continued pre-training as a model-customization method for using unlabeled data to enhance domain knowledge.

questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon Bedrock for a generative AI solution. The solution must integrate with a service that provides vector database storage and vector-search capabilities. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service supports storing vector embeddings and performing vector similarity searches, and it integrates with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI and knowledge-base workloads. Vector search – Amazon OpenSearch Service
learnMore: Vector search – Amazon OpenSearch Service
Turning data into a knowledge base – Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A retail store wants to predict the demand for a specific product for the next few weeks by using the Amazon SageMaker DeepAR forecasting algorithm. Which type of data will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: The Amazon SageMaker DeepAR forecasting algorithm is specifically designed for time series forecasting tasks. It requires historical time-series data (observations collected at regular intervals, such as daily or weekly sales figures) to learn patterns and trends in order to predict future demand values. Text, image, and binary data are not suitable for this algorithm.
learnMore: Use the SageMaker DeepAR forecasting algorithm

questions.questionText: An ecommerce company wants to group customers according to their purchase history and preferences in order to personalize the user experience in the company’s application. Which ML technique should the company use?
questions.explanation: Clustering is an unsupervised machine learning technique that groups customers with similar purchase histories and preferences into segments, enabling personalized application experiences.
learnMore: K-Means Algorithm - Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of structured data?
options: A. A file of text comments from an online forum
B. A compilation of video files that contains news broadcasts
C. A CSV file that consists of measurement data
D. Transcribed conversations between call center agents and customers
questions.explanation: A CSV file organizes measurement values into consistent rows and columns, giving the data a defined tabular structure that can be readily parsed and queried.

questions.questionText: An e-commerce company is deploying a chatbot. The chatbot will allow users to ask questions about the company’s products and receive details about users’ orders. The company must implement safeguards that filter harmful content from input prompts and chatbot responses. Which AWS feature or resource meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provides configurable content filters that detect and filter harmful content in both user prompts and model-generated responses, making it the appropriate safety control for the chatbot.
learnMore: Detect and filter harmful content by using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

questions.questionText: A customer service team is building an application to analyze customer feedback and automatically categorize that feedback. The categories include product quality, customer service, and delivery experience. Which AI concept does this scenario represent?
questions.explanation: Natural language processing (NLP) enables systems to interpret, analyze, and classify human-written text, including categorizing customer feedback by its subject or sentiment.
learnMore: What is Natural Language Processing? - AWS

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A financial company wants to create workflows for human review of ML predictions. The company wants to set confidence thresholds for its use case and modify those thresholds over time. Which AWS service satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I) provides human review workflows for machine learning predictions. It supports configuring confidence-based conditions that trigger human review and updating those thresholds as the use case changes.
learnMore: Reviewing inappropriate content with Amazon Augmented AI
Create a Human Review Workflow

questions.questionText: A financial institution is building an AI solution to make loan approval decisions by using a foundation model (FM). For security and audit purposes, the company needs the AI solution's decisions to be explainable. Which factor relates to the explainability of the AI solution's decisions?
questions.explanation: Model complexity directly determines how interpretable and explainable AI decisions are. Simpler models like logistic regression or decision trees allow clear tracing of how inputs lead to decisions, making them suitable for high-stakes applications like loan approval where audit trails are critical. More complex models, particularly deep neural networks, function as black boxes and obscure the reasoning behind predictions. Training time, hyperparameter count, and deployment time do not meaningfully affect explainability.

Model Explainability - Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner needs to evaluate ML models and provide explanations of model predictions to customers and stakeholders. Which AWS service or feature meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Clarify explains ML model predictions using model-agnostic feature attribution, enabling stakeholders and customers to understand why a model produced a result. It supports both overall model understanding and per-instance prediction explanations.
learnMore: Model Explainability - Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company wants to develop a large language model (LLM) application by using Amazon Bedrock and customer data that is uploaded to Amazon S3. The company's security policy states that each team can access data for only the team's own customers. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon Bedrock custom service role for each team that has access to only the team's customer data.
B. Create a custom service role that has Amazon S3 access. Ask teams to specify the customer name on each Amazon Bedrock request.
C. Redact personal data in Amazon S3. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow team access to customer data.
D. Create one Amazon Bedrock role that has full Amazon S3 access. Create IAM roles for each team that have access to only each team's customer folders.
questions.explanation: Each team requires its own Amazon Bedrock service role with fine-grained permissions restricting access only to that team's customer data folders and resources. This enforces the principle of least privilege at the service level. Creating a single Bedrock role with full S3 access violates security policy; relying on teams to self-specify customer names provides no enforcement mechanism; data redaction alone doesn't solve access control requirements.
learnMore: Service roles for Amazon Bedrock
Identity and access management for Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company wants to integrate an AI solution that contacts emergency services within 30 seconds after detecting a vehicle crash. The company intends to use a pre-trained model with no additional training. Which factor should the company prioritize when choosing a model to satisfy these requirements?
questions.explanation: Model size directly affects inference latency and compute requirements. Selecting an appropriately smaller pre-trained model helps achieve the strict 30-second response-time requirement without requiring additional training.
learnMore: AI Practitioner exam guide - Domain 3: foundation model selection criteria
Optimize model inference for latency (Amazon Bedrock)

questions.questionText: A healthcare company is developing an AI solution to predict patient readmission within 30 days after discharge. The company has trained a model on historical patient data, including medical history, demographics, and treatment specifications, to generate real-time readmission predictions. Which task represents AI model inference in this scenario?
options: A. Gather historical patient readmission data.
B. Use appropriate metrics and assess model performance.
C. Use data to identify patient patterns and correlations.
D. Use a trained model to predict patient readmission.
questions.explanation: AI model inference is the use of a trained machine-learning model with input data to generate a prediction or output. Applying the trained model to patient data to predict readmission is therefore inference.
learnMore: Run AI/ML inference workloads on Amazon EKS

questions.questionText: Which technique trains AI models using labeled datasets to adapt them to particular industry terminology and requirements?
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning further trains a pretrained model on labeled domain- or task-specific examples, enabling it to learn specialized terminology and meet particular requirements.
learnMore: Customize a model with fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company wants to enhance multiple ML models.
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant external data and supplies it as context to an LLM at inference time. Zero-shot learning performs a task without task-specific examples, whereas few-shot learning relies on a small number of examples. Fine-tuning instead updates a pretrained model using additional training data.

questions.questionText: A company wants to improve its chatbot responses so they align with the company’s desired tone. The company has 100 examples of high-quality conversations between customer service agents and customers. The company wants to use this data to incorporate the company tone into the chatbot’s responses. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon Personalize to generate responses.
B. Create an Amazon SageMaker HyperPod pre-training job.
C. Host the model by using Amazon SageMaker. Use TensorRT for large language model (LLM) deployment.
D. Create an Amazon Bedrock fine-tuning job.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock fine-tuning creates a customized model by training a foundation model on the company’s example conversations, allowing the model to learn the desired response style and tone. AWS documents that a fine-tuning job customizes a base model using specified training data.
learnMore: CreateModelCustomizationJob - Amazon Bedrock API Reference
Customize a model with fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company wants to use a pre-trained generative AI model to generate content for its marketing campaigns. The company needs to ensure that the generated content aligns with the company's brand voice and messaging requirements. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Optimize the model's architecture and hyperparameters to improve the model's overall performance.
B. Increase the model's complexity by adding more layers to the model's architecture.
C. Create effective prompts that provide clear instructions and context to guide the model's generation.
D. Select a large, diverse dataset to pre-train a new generative model.
questions.explanation: Prompt engineering—crafting detailed prompts with clear instructions and context—is the most effective way to guide a pre-trained model to generate content aligned with brand voice and messaging without modifying the underlying model.
learnMore: Prompt engineering concepts (Amazon Bedrock)

questions.questionText: A company needs to choose a model from Amazon Bedrock to use internally. The company must identify a model that generates responses in a style that the company's employees prefer. What should the company do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Evaluate the models by using built-in prompt datasets.
B. Evaluate the models by using a human workforce and custom prompt datasets.
C. Use public model leaderboards to identify the model.
D. Use the model InvocationLatency runtime metrics in Amazon CloudWatch when trying models.
questions.explanation: Evaluating models with human workforce and custom prompt datasets tailored to the company's specific needs ensures the selected model matches employee preferences for response style. Generic built-in datasets or public leaderboards cannot measure subjective alignment with internal requirements.
learnMore: Model evaluation jobs that use human workers
Evaluate the performance of Amazon Bedrock resources

questions.questionText: A human resources company is developing an AI/ML solution to screen resumes and choose relevant applicants for various job roles. Which AI methodologies can help ensure impartial treatment of all demographic groups? Choose two
questions.explanation: Fairness evaluates and mitigates biased model outcomes across demographic groups. Explainability makes selection decisions interpretable and auditable, which helps detect and address discriminatory factors or proxies in the screening process.
learnMore: Responsible AI - Generative AI Lens
Core dimensions of responsible AI

questions.questionText: A retail company wants to develop an ML model that recommends products to customers. The company wants to build the model using responsible practices. Which practice should the company use when collecting data to reduce model bias?
options: A. Use data from only customers who match the demographics of the company's overall customer base.
B. Collect data from customers who have a past purchase history.
C. Ensure that the data is balanced and collected from a diverse group.
D. Ensure that the data is from a publicly available dataset.
questions.explanation: Balanced data collected from a diverse, representative group helps prevent systematic overrepresentation or underrepresentation of customer groups, reducing the risk of biased model outcomes. Microsoft guidance identifies diverse and representative training data as a fairness practice to minimize bias.
learnMore: Apply responsible AI principles
Understand your datasets - Azure Machine Learning

questions.questionText: A company notices that its foundation model (FM) generates images that are unrelated to the prompts. The company wants to modify the prompt techniques to decrease unrelated images. Which solution meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Negative prompts explicitly specify what should not be included in the generated images, helping the model focus on desired attributes and filter out unrelated content. This technique directly addresses the problem of random or irrelevant image generation by constraining the output space. Zero-shot and positive prompts alone provide less explicit guidance on what to avoid, while ambiguous prompts would worsen the issue.
learnMore: Stability AI models on Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: Which situation illustrates a possible risk and limitation of prompt engineering when using a generative AI model?
options: A. Prompt engineering does not ensure that the model always produces consistent and deterministic outputs, eliminating the need for validation.
B. Prompt engineering could expose the model to vulnerabilities such as prompt injection attacks.
C. Properly designed prompts reduce but do not eliminate the risk of data poisoning or model hijacking.
D. Prompt engineering does not ensure that the model will consistently generate highly reliable outputs when working with real-world data.
questions.explanation: Prompt injection is a security vulnerability in which malicious instructions embedded in user-controlled or external content attempt to override intended model behavior. Prompt engineering alone cannot guarantee protection against these attacks.
learnMore: Prompt injection security (Amazon Bedrock)
Detect prompt attacks with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

questions.questionText: Which choice is an example of unsupervised learning?
options: A. Clustering data points into groups based on their similarity
B. Training a model to recognize images of animals
C. Predicting the price of a house based on the house’s features
D. Generating human-like text based on a given prompt
questions.explanation: Unsupervised learning discovers structure in unlabeled data. Clustering organizes data points into similarity-based groups without requiring known output labels.
learnMore: Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning - AWS

questions.questionText: An ecommerce company uses a generative AI chatbot to answer customer inquiries. The company wants to measure the chatbot’s financial impact on its operations. Which metric should the company use?
options: A. Number of customer inquiries handled
B. Cost of training AI models
C. Cost for each customer conversation
questions.explanation: Cost for each customer conversation directly measures the operational cost of serving customers through the chatbot and supports evaluation of its financial impact.
learnMore: Generative AI pricing model (AWS Well-Architected)
Optimizing costs of generative AI applications on AWS

questions.questionText: A company developed a large language model (LLM) and wants to make it available to several internal teams. The company must choose the appropriate inference mode for each team.
questions.explanation: Real-time inference serves interactive requests with low latency, so it fits both the chatbot and the API that processes small text payloads. Batch transform is intended for offline inference on large datasets and does not require a persistent endpoint, so it fits processing gigabytes of files on weekends.
learnMore: Supported features - Amazon SageMaker AI
Batch transform for inference with Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: Which prompting attack directly exposes the configured behavior of a large language model (LLM)?
questions.explanation: Extracting the prompt template is a prompting attack that directly reveals the underlying configured behavior, instructions, or system prompts of an LLM. This exposes how the model has been configured and designed to respond, giving attackers insight into the model's constraints and behavioral instructions. The other options involve manipulating the model's behavior (persona switches, friendliness exploitation) or ignoring prompts, but they do not directly expose the configured behavior itself.
learnMore: LLM07:2025 System Prompt Leakage - OWASP Gen AI Security Project
Designing for the inevitable: system prompt leakage and mitigations

questions.questionText: A company wants to create an application by using Amazon Bedrock. The company has a limited budget and prefers flexibility without long-term commitment. Which Amazon Bedrock pricing model meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: On-Demand pricing for Amazon Bedrock requires no long-term commitment and charges only for actual usage, providing maximum flexibility and cost control for companies with limited budgets and variable workloads. Model customization is a feature, not a pricing model. Provisioned Throughput requires capacity reservations (long-term commitment), and Spot Instance is an EC2 concept not applicable to Bedrock.

questions.questionText: Which technique divides a complex task into smaller subtasks that are submitted sequentially to a large language model (LLM)?
questions.explanation: Prompt chaining breaks a complex workflow into sequential subtasks, with each LLM output able to inform the next prompt in the chain.
learnMore: Perform AI prompt-chaining with Amazon Bedrock (Step Functions)
Build and orchestrate generative AI applications with Amazon Bedrock

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company has obtained access to Amazon Bedrock to build applications. The company needs to limit employee access to particular models available in Amazon Bedrock. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies to restrict model access.
B. Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to generate temporary credentials for model use.
C. Use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) service roles to restrict model subscription.
D. Use Amazon Inspector to monitor model access.
questions.explanation: IAM policies enforce least-privilege access by granting or denying Amazon Bedrock model-invocation actions against specified foundation-model ARNs. AWS documentation states that access can be restricted to a specific model by using that model’s ARN in the IAM policy resource.
learnMore: Identity-based policy examples for Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A healthcare company needs to analyze patient data. The data was collected during the previous year to identify patterns in disease outbreaks. The company must produce a monthly trend-analysis report to present to public health officials. It must also provide insights from patient data for the most recent month of the current year. Which inference method will satisfy these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?
questions.explanation: Batch transform is designed for offline inference over an entire dataset and does not require a continuously running endpoint. It is well suited to scheduled monthly trend analysis of historical patient data, making it more cost-effective than inference methods intended for low-latency or continuously available predictions.
learnMore: Batch transform for inference - Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: A company is implementing intelligent agents to provide conversational search experiences for its customers. The company needs a database service that will support storage and queries of embeddings from a generative AI model as vectors in the database. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL supports the pgvector extension, which enables efficient storage and similarity-based queries of vector embeddings. This is essential for conversational search and intelligent agent systems that leverage embeddings from generative AI models. Amazon Athena is a query service without vector support, Redshift is for data warehousing, and EMR is for distributed processing—none provide native vector database functionality.
learnMore: Using Aurora PostgreSQL as a Knowledge Base for Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: An education provider is building a question and answer application that uses a generative AI model to explain complex concepts. The education provider wants to automatically change the style of the model response depending on who is asking the question. The education provider will give the model the age range of the user who has asked the question. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?
options: A. Fine-tune the model by using additional training data that is representative of the various age ranges that the application will support.
B. Add a role description to the prompt context that instructs the model of the age range that the response should target.
C. Use chain-of-thought reasoning to deduce the correct style and complexity for a response suitable for that user.
D. Summarize the response text depending on the age of the user so that younger users receive shorter responses.
questions.explanation: Prompt engineering with role descriptions requires minimal implementation effort—adding context like "explain this concept for a 10-year-old" to the prompt guides the model to adjust tone and complexity automatically. This leverages the model's existing capabilities without retraining. Fine-tuning requires substantial labeled data and compute; chain-of-thought reasoning adds inference time without ensuring appropriateness; post-hoc response summarization is less direct.
learnMore: Prompt engineering concepts (persona/role) - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: Which task represents a use case for intelligent document processing (IDP)?
options: C. Analyze user feedback and perform sentiment analysis
D. Automatically extract and format data from scanned files
questions.explanation: Intelligent document processing uses AI and OCR capabilities to extract text, handwriting, layout elements, and structured data from scanned documents, such as forms, tables, PDFs, and images. Amazon Textract

questions.questionText: A company wants to deploy a conversational chatbot to answer customer questions. The chatbot is based on a fine-tuned Amazon SageMaker JumpStart model. The application must comply with multiple regulatory frameworks. Which capabilities can the company show compliance for? Choose two
questions.explanation: Threat detection and data protection are the two capabilities directly aligned with regulatory compliance frameworks. Threat detection (e.g., AWS GuardDuty) identifies unauthorized access and attacks, while data protection via encryption and access controls safeguards sensitive customer information. Auto-scaling optimizes performance/cost, cost optimization manages expenses, and loosely coupled microservices are architectural patterns—these don't address regulatory compliance requirements.

Compliance validation for Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: A financial company is building a generative AI application to make loan-approval decisions. The company requires the application's output to be responsible and fair. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Review the training data to check for biases. Include data from all demographics in the training data.
B. Use a deep learning model with many hidden layers.
C. Keep the model’s decision-making process a secret to protect proprietary algorithms.
D. Continuously monitor the model’s performance on a static test dataset
questions.explanation: Reviewing training data for bias and including data representing all demographics helps reduce discriminatory outcomes in loan-approval decisions and supports fair, responsible AI.
learnMore: Fairness and bias detection with SageMaker Clarify

questions.questionText: A company wants to build an interpretable ML model to evaluate the risk of loan applications. Which ML model type or algorithm meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Logistic regression is an interpretable supervised model for binary outcomes such as loan risk. Its feature coefficients show the direction and relative influence of each input on the predicted probability, supporting transparent risk assessments.
learnMore: Linear Learner Algorithm (Amazon SageMaker)
Interpretability on AWS

questions.questionText: Which strategy will determine if a foundation model (FM) effectively meets business objectives?
options: A. Evaluate the model's performance on benchmark datasets.
B. Analyze the model's architecture and hyperparameters.
C. Assess the model's alignment with specific use cases.
D. Measure the computational resources required for model deployment.
questions.explanation: To determine if a foundation model meets business objectives, it must be assessed for alignment with specific use cases and real-world applications relevant to the business. This direct evaluation ensures the model produces valuable, actionable outputs for the organization's goals. While benchmark performance (A), architecture analysis (B), and resource measurement (D) are useful, they do not directly validate whether the model solves the intended business problem.
learnMore: What are foundation model evaluations?

questions.questionText: A company is developing an AI solution using Amazon SageMaker AI and wants to use SageMaker AI features to support application development.
questions.explanation: SageMaker Model Cards documents a model’s intended use, evaluation results, and business-goal alignment. Data Wrangler provides visual data preparation with little to no coding. SageMaker Clarify measures bias in raw training data, including class and label imbalance.
learnMore: Prepare ML Data with Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler

questions.questionText: A company intends to use a generative AI model to deliver real-time service quotes to users. Which criterion should the company use to choose the correct model for this use case?
options: C. General-purpose use and high-powered GPU availability
D. Model latency and optimized inference speed
questions.explanation: Real-time generative AI applications require low-latency responses. Model latency and optimized inference speed determine whether service quotes can be generated quickly enough for an interactive user experience. AWS guidance identifies inference latency as critical for real-time applications.
learnMore: Performance efficiency - Generative AI Lens
Choosing models for generative AI applications

questions.questionText: What does an F1 score evaluate in the context of foundation model (FM) performance?
options: B. Model speed in generating responses
C. Financial cost of operating the model
D. Energy efficiency of the model’s computations
questions.explanation: An F1 score combines precision and recall through their harmonic mean, measuring how well predictions balance correctness among positive predictions with coverage of actual positive cases.
learnMore: Metrics and validation (Amazon SageMaker Autopilot)
Binary Model Insights (Amazon Machine Learning)

questions.questionText: A bank has fine-tuned a large language model (LLM) to expedite the loan approval process. During an external audit of the model, the company discovered that the model was approving loans at a faster pace for a specific demographic than for other demographics. How should the bank fix this issue MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Include more diverse training data. Fine-tune the model again by using the new data.
B. Use Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with the fine-tuned model.
C. Use AWS Trusted Advisor checks to eliminate bias.
D. Pre-train a new LLM with more diverse training data.
questions.explanation: The demographic disparity in loan approvals most likely stems from an unrepresentative training set, so augmenting the data with more diverse examples and re-fine-tuning the existing model directly targets the root cause at a fraction of the cost of pre-training a brand-new foundation model. Retrieval Augmented Generation only supplements the model's context at inference time and does not correct bias already learned in the model's weights, and AWS Trusted Advisor has no capability to detect or remediate model bias.

questions.questionText: A company is developing a new generative AI chatbot. The chatbot uses an Amazon Bedrock foundation model (FM) to generate responses. During testing, the company finds that the chatbot is susceptible to prompt injection attacks. What can the company do to secure the chatbot with the LEAST implementation effort?
options: A. Fine-tune the FM to avoid harmful responses.
B. Use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails content filters and denied topics.
C. Change the FM to a more secure FM.
D. Use chain-of-thought prompting to produce secure responses.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provides managed content filters that can detect and filter prompt attacks, including prompt injection, in user inputs and model responses. Denied topics can also block application-specific undesirable topics, making Guardrails the lowest-effort built-in protection among the available approaches.

questions.questionText: A financial company is building a fraud-detection system that identifies potential fraud in credit card transactions. Employees will review the fraud cases that are flagged. The company wants to minimize the time employees spend reviewing flagged fraud cases that are not truly fraudulent. Which evaluation metric satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Precision is the proportion of transactions flagged as fraud that are actually fraudulent. Maximizing precision reduces false-positive fraud alerts, so employees spend less time investigating legitimate transactions.
learnMore: Binary Model Insights – Precision (Amazon Machine Learning)
Detect fraudulent transactions using ML with Amazon SageMaker

questions.questionText: A medical company wants to modernize its on-site information-processing application. The company wants to use generative AI to answer patients' medical questions. Which AWS service should the company use to help ensure responsible AI for the application?
questions.explanation: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock provides configurable safety and privacy controls for generative-AI applications, including filters for harmful content, denied topics, and sensitive information in user inputs and model responses. These safeguards support responsible AI when responding to patient medical questions.
learnMore: Detect and filter harmful content by using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company must meet regulatory standards when developing and using trustworthy AI management solutions. Which approach satisfies this requirement?
options: A. Optimize model inference time by using high-powered GPUs for faster processing.
B. Ensure that each AI solution is developed only by technical experts. Do not involve other stakeholders.
C. Constrain transparency and user access to each model’s decision-making process.
D. Ensure fairness, transparency, accountability, and security throughout the lifecycle of each AI solution.
questions.explanation: Trustworthy AI requires responsible-AI practices throughout the lifecycle, including fairness, transparency, accountability, and security. These principles support equitable outcomes, explainability and auditability, clear governance, and protection of systems and data.
learnMore: What is Responsible AI?
Artificial Intelligence overview - Microsoft Service Assurance

questions.questionText: Which AWS service or feature can help an AI development team quickly deploy and consume a foundation model (FM) within the team's VPC?
options: C. PartyRock, an Amazon Bedrock Playground
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart offers a curated hub of publicly available and proprietary foundation models that can be launched with just a few clicks into endpoints hosted inside the team's own VPC, making it purpose-built for quickly deploying and consuming an FM. SageMaker endpoints are merely the underlying hosting resource that JumpStart (and other workflows) provision — using them directly still requires sourcing, packaging, and configuring the model yourself, which is slower and not what the option describes.

questions.questionText: A company has a generative AI application that uses a pre-trained foundation model (FM) in Amazon Bedrock. The company wants the FM to incorporate additional context by using company information. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?
options: A. Use Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases.
B. Choose a different FM on Amazon Bedrock.
D. Deploy a custom model on Amazon Bedrock.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases provides a managed RAG capability that retrieves relevant information from company data sources and supplies it as context for generated responses. It is more cost-effective than continually training or deploying a custom model to use private data.
learnMore: How Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases work

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company wants to implement a data-governance framework for its AI system. The framework must enable the company to monitor when data is created, updated, and scheduled for deletion. Which data-governance component satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Data lifecycle management governs data from creation through transformation, retention, and disposal. It supports retention and deletion policies, including tracking when data is created or changed and when it is due to be deleted.

questions.questionText: A company wants to categorize human genes into 20 groups according to their gene characteristics. The company requires an ML algorithm that can document how the model’s internal mechanism influences its output. Which ML algorithm satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Decision trees support multiclass classification and make predictions through explicit feature-based split rules. Those paths and rules can be inspected and documented to show how the model’s internal logic produces each output.

questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to build, deploy, and implement agents at scale. For each description, select the correct AgentCore resource. Select each resource once or not at all.
questions.explanation: AgentCore Observability provides dashboards and telemetry to trace, debug, and monitor agent behavior. AgentCore Code Interpreter executes code securely in isolated sandbox environments and supports multiple programming languages. AgentCore Browser Tool provides a secure, managed browser environment for agent web interactions.
learnMore: Observe your agent applications on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Observability

questions.questionText: A company has an ML model and wants to understand how the model produces predictions. Which term refers to understanding model predictions?
questions.explanation: Model interpretability is the ability to understand and explain how a machine learning model produces its predictions.
learnMore: Interpretability on AWS
Model explainability with SageMaker Clarify

questions.questionText: A company wants to use large language models (LLMs) with Amazon Bedrock to develop a chat interface for the company's product manuals. The manuals are stored as PDF files. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Use prompt engineering to add one PDF file as context to the user prompt when the prompt is submitted to Amazon Bedrock.
B. Use prompt engineering to add all the PDF files as context to the user prompt when the prompt is submitted to Amazon Bedrock.
C. Use all the PDF documents to fine-tune a model with Amazon Bedrock. Use the fine-tuned model to process user prompts.
D. Upload PDF documents to an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. Use the knowledge base to provide context when users submit prompts to Amazon Bedrock.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base implements Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), enabling efficient cost-effective augmentation of foundation models with proprietary PDF content. The knowledge base retrieves only relevant context per query, avoiding the token cost and latency of including all PDFs in every prompt or the expense of fine-tuning on the entire document set.

questions.questionText: Which type of ML technique offers the MOST explainability?
questions.explanation: Linear regression is highly interpretable because its learned coefficients directly show how each input feature affects the predicted value. AWS guidance notes that linear-regression coefficient magnitudes provide global feature importance, and a feature’s coefficient multiplied by its value provides a local attribution.
learnMore: Overview of machine learning model interpretability

questions.questionText: Which AWS feature captures details about ML instance data for governance and reporting?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards provide a standardized way to document machine learning model details for governance and reporting, such as training information, evaluation results, intended uses, and risk assessments.

questions.questionText: A manufacturing company uses AI to inspect products and find any damages or defects. Which type of AI application is the company using?
questions.explanation: Computer vision is the field of artificial intelligence that enables machines to interpret, analyze, and make decisions based on visual data from images or videos. Product inspection for defects and damages is a classic computer vision application that uses object detection and anomaly detection algorithms. Recommendation systems (A) personalize suggestions, NLP (B) processes text, and image processing (D) is lower-level signal processing rather than decision-making AI.
learnMore: What is Computer Vision?

questions.questionText: Which term describes the numerical representations of real-world objects and concepts that AI and natural language processing (NLP) models use to improve understanding of textual information?
questions.explanation: Embeddings are dense numerical vectors that represent words, phrases, or concepts in continuous space, capturing semantic relationships and meaning. AI and NLP models use embeddings to improve understanding and processing of textual information.
learnMore: What is Embedding? (AWS)

questions.questionText: A company is developing a new model to predict the prices of specific items. The model performed well on the training dataset. When the company deployed the model to production, the model's performance decreased significantly. What should the company do to mitigate this problem?
options: A. Reduce the volume of data that is used in training.
B. Add hyperparameters to the model.
C. Increase the volume of data that is used in training.
D. Increase the model training time.
questions.explanation: The performance gap between training and production typically indicates overfitting—the model learned training data too closely and fails to generalize. Increasing the volume of training data provides more diverse examples that prevent overfitting and improve generalization to unseen production data. Reducing data or increasing training time would worsen the problem; adding hyperparameters doesn't address the root cause.
learnMore: Model Fit: Underfitting vs. Overfitting
What is Overfitting?

questions.questionText: Which scenario is a practical application of generative AI?
options: A. Using an ML model to forecast product demand
B. Employing a chatbot to provide human-like responses to customer queries in real time
C. Using an analytics dashboard to track website traffic and user behavior
D. Implementing a rule-based recommendation engine to suggest products to customers
questions.explanation: Generative AI chatbots use large language models to generate non-scripted, human-like responses to customer inputs in real time. Demand forecasting is predictive machine learning, analytics dashboards report data, and rule-based recommendation engines use predefined rules rather than generative models.
learnMore: Google Cloud: AI chatbot

questions.questionText: An ecommerce company is developing a generative AI solution that creates personalized product recommendations for application users. The company wants to measure how effectively the AI solution improves product sales and user engagement in the application.
questions.explanation: Click-through rate measures engagement with recommendation links or placements. Average order value measures the monetary value of purchases per order, and retention rate measures whether users return over time.
learnMore: Measure the business impact of Amazon Personalize recommendations
Measuring recommendation impact with A/B testing

questions.questionText: A company plans to fine-tune a foundation model (FM) to answer questions in a particular domain. The company intends to use instruction-based fine-tuning. How should the company prepare its training data?
options: A. Gather company internal documents and industry-specific materials. Merge the documents and materials into a single file.
B. Collect external company reviews from various online sources. Manually label each review as either positive or negative.
C. Create pairs of questions and answers that specifically address topics related to the company's industry domain.
D. Create few-shot prompts to instruct the model to answer only domain knowledge.
questions.explanation: Instruction-based fine-tuning uses supervised prompt–completion examples. For domain question answering, each example should contain a domain-relevant question as the prompt and its expected answer as the completion, so the model learns the required response behavior. Amazon Bedrock documents fine-tuning datasets for question answering as prompt and completion pairs.
learnMore: Prepare data for fine-tuning your models - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company is developing a generative AI application to help customers make travel reservations. The application will handle customer requests and invoke the appropriate API calls to complete reservation transactions. Which Amazon Bedrock resource meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Agents can interpret customer requests, break work into steps, and use action groups to invoke APIs that complete actions in external systems, including travel-reservation transactions.
learnMore: Automate tasks in your application using AI agents

questions.questionText: A company wants to use a large language model (LLM) on Amazon Bedrock for sentiment analysis. The company wants to classify the sentiment of text passages as positive or negative. Which prompt engineering strategy meets these requirements?
options: A. Provide examples of text passages with corresponding positive or negative labels in the prompt followed by the new text passage to be classified.
B. Provide a detailed explanation of sentiment analysis and how LLMs work in the prompt.
C. Provide the new text passage to be classified without any additional context or examples.
D. Provide the new text passage with a few examples of unrelated tasks, such as text summarization or question answering.
questions.explanation: This approach uses few-shot prompting, a proven technique where labeled examples guide the model on the desired task format. Providing examples of text passages with positive/negative labels helps the model understand the classification task and generate accurate predictions on new input. Explaining sentiment analysis concepts is unnecessary (the model needs examples, not theory), classification without examples or context reduces accuracy, and unrelated task examples would confuse the model.

Few-shot prompt engineering and fine-tuning for LLMs in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: Which option is a use case for generative AI models?
options: A. Improving network security by using intrusion detection systems
B. Creating photorealistic images from text descriptions for digital marketing
C. Enhancing database performance by using optimized indexing
D. Analyzing financial data to forecast stock market trends
questions.explanation: Creating photorealistic images from text descriptions is a quintessential generative AI use case, exemplified by models like DALL-E and Stable Diffusion. Generative AI models are specifically designed to create new content—images, text, audio, and code—based on input descriptions. Option A involves classification (discriminative), Option C is database optimization (not AI), and Option D is predictive analytics (not generative).
learnMore: What is Generative AI?

questions.questionText: A company wants to improve the response quality of a large language model (LLM) for complex problem-solving tasks. These tasks require detailed reasoning and a step-by-step explanation process. Which prompt-engineering technique fulfills these requirements?
questions.explanation: Chain-of-thought prompting guides an LLM to produce intermediate reasoning steps, making it suited to complex problem-solving tasks that require detailed, step-by-step explanations.
learnMore: Prompt engineering concepts - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company is developing a large language model (LLM)-based AI assistant to help service agents automatically manage customer inquiries. The company aims to reduce the effort customer service agents need during support calls. The company must choose a metric to evaluate the AI assistant against one of its business objectives. Which metric meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Average call duration directly reflects the time and effort agents spend on support calls. Lowering it indicates that the AI assistant is helping agents handle customer inquiries more efficiently. Amazon Connect defines average conversation duration as the average duration of voice contacts with agents.
learnMore: Conversational analytics metrics in Amazon Connect

questions.questionText: A digital devices company wants to predict customer demand for memory hardware. The company does not have coding experience or knowledge of ML algorithms and needs to develop a data-driven predictive model. The company needs to perform analysis on internal data and external data. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Store the data in Amazon S3. Create ML models and demand forecast predictions by using Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithms that use the data from Amazon S3.
B. Import the data into Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. Create ML models and demand forecast predictions by using SageMaker built-in algorithms.
C. Import the data into Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. Build ML models and demand forecast predictions by using an Amazon Personalize Trending-Now recipe.
D. Import the data into Amazon SageMaker Canvas. Build ML models and demand forecast predictions by selecting the values in the data from SageMaker Canvas.
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Canvas is a no-code machine learning service designed for users without coding or ML expertise, enabling visual model building, data analysis, and prediction generation through an intuitive graphical interface. It directly supports both internal and external data integration. SageMaker built-in algorithms and Data Wrangler require technical expertise; Personalize targets recommendation engines rather than demand forecasting.

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner uses an Amazon Nova text model and wants to apply prompt-engineering techniques that support iterative refinement.
questions.explanation: A task defines the intended use case; a role establishes the model persona; response style controls tone, format, and structure; and success criteria define how output quality is evaluated.

Design a prompt

questions.questionText: A company wants to make a chatbot to help customers. The chatbot will help solve technical problems without human intervention. The company chose a foundation model (FM) for the chatbot. The chatbot needs to produce responses that adhere to company tone. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Set a low limit on the number of tokens the FM can produce.
B. Use batch inferencing to process detailed responses.
C. Experiment and refine the prompt until the FM produces the desired responses.
D. Define a higher number for the temperature parameter.
questions.explanation: Prompt engineering through iterative refinement is the most effective way to guide a foundation model to produce responses adhering to company tone and style. By carefully crafting and testing prompts, practitioners can set clear expectations and context for the model's behavior without requiring retraining. Token limits don't control tone, batch processing affects throughput not behavior, and higher temperature increases randomness rather than tone alignment.

questions.questionText: A company uses foundation models (FMs) to automate daily tasks. An AI practitioner at the company is developing system instructions that contain context relevant to those tasks. The AI practitioner wants to save and reuse the instructions in daily interactions with FMs in Amazon Bedrock. Which Amazon Bedrock solution meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Prompt management lets practitioners create, save, version, and reuse prompts across workflows. Its prompts can include system instructions and contextual content for supported models, making it the appropriate solution for reusable daily FM interactions.
learnMore: Construct and store reusable prompts with Prompt management in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company manually reviews all submitted resumes in PDF format. As the company grows, the company expects the volume of resumes to exceed the company's review capacity. The company needs an automated system to convert the PDF resumes into plain text format for additional processing. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Textract is a fully managed document analysis service that automatically extracts text and structured data from PDFs, including embedded text in tables and forms. It is purpose-built for converting scanned/PDF resumes into plain text for downstream processing.

questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon Bedrock to build an assistant for its online store. The company needs to ensure that the assistant does not generate harmful responses involving hate speech, insults, sexual content, or violence. Which strategy will prevent harmful responses in Amazon Bedrock?
options: A. Use Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithms to filter harmful content.
B. Use Amazon Comprehend toxicity detection to identify harmful content.
C. Configure Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock to filter harmful content.
D. Train a custom model according to the company’s responsible AI policies.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails includes configurable content filters that detect and filter harmful model responses in the Hate, Insults, Sexual, and Violence categories. Filter strengths can be configured for each category to block undesirable generated content.
learnMore: Detect and filter harmful content by using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

questions.questionText: A company has built a generative AI application using Amazon Bedrock. The application generates catalogs that are refreshed weekly. The company must choose a pricing model for the weekly catalog refreshes. Which Amazon Bedrock pricing model satisfies these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock batch inference is designed for asynchronous, bulk, non-time-sensitive inference workloads. Weekly catalog generation can be submitted as a batch job, avoiding the cost of continuously reserved capacity and making Batch the most cost-effective option.

questions.explanation: A context window is the maximum amount of input context a model can process in a prompt. Latency measures the time taken to return generated output. Concurrency is the number of simultaneous requests or users an endpoint can serve.

Optimize model inference for latency - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company requires its AI models to be transparent and explainable. Which combination of Amazon SageMaker AI features meets these requirements? Choose two
questions.explanation: SageMaker Model Cards centralize documentation of critical model details for governance, reporting, auditing, and responsible AI practices, supporting transparency. SageMaker Clarify explains model predictions through feature attributions, supporting explainability.
learnMore: Model Explainability - Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: A research company is cultivating microbiological cultures. It captures images of those cultures without having any preexisting labeled data about growth areas. The company needs to identify image regions that display culture growth. Which ML technique meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Clustering is an unsupervised learning technique that groups similar observations without labeled training data. It can separate image regions with similar visual characteristics, enabling identification of regions associated with culture growth.

K-means algorithm (Amazon SageMaker AI)

questions.questionText: A company needs to label training datasets using human feedback in order to fine-tune a foundation model (FM). The company does not want to build labeling applications or manage a labeling workforce. Which AWS service or feature fulfills these requirements?
options: B. Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth Plus
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth Plus is a turnkey managed data-labeling service that supplies and manages an expert workforce and labeling workflows. It supports preparing human-feedback and fine-tuning datasets for foundation models without requiring the customer to develop labeling applications or operate the labeling workforce.
learnMore: Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth Plus to Label Data

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner with minimal ML knowledge wants to predict employee attrition without writing code. Which Amazon SageMaker feature fulfills this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Canvas provides a visual no-code machine learning experience for users without extensive ML expertise. It can build and use custom models for categorical predictions, including a two-category outcome such as employee attrition.
learnMore: Automated ML, no-code, or low-code

questions.questionText: A medical company needs to build an AI application that can access structured patient records, extract relevant details, and create concise summaries. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to extract relevant medical entities and relationships. Apply rule-based logic to structure and format summaries.
B. Use Amazon Personalize to analyze patient engagement patterns. Integrate the output with a general purpose text summarization tool.
C. Use Amazon Textract to convert scanned documents into digital text. Design a keyword extraction system to generate summaries.
D. Implement Amazon Kendra to provide a searchable index for medical records. Use a template-based system to format summaries.
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend Medical detects medical entities such as conditions, medications, tests, treatments, and related attributes in clinical content. Its entity and relationship output can be used by rule-based logic to assemble a concise, structured summary.
