questions.questionText: A company has fine-tuned an Amazon Bedrock foundation model (FM) to generate short document summaries. The company needs an automated metric that compares every model-generated summary with its human-authored reference summary. Which metric satisfies these requirements?
options: B. Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE)
questions.explanation: ROUGE evaluates summarization quality by comparing overlapping word units, such as n-grams or longest common subsequences, between a generated summary and its ground-truth reference summary. AWS documentation identifies ROUGE as a summarization metric for this generated-versus-reference comparison.
learnMore: Accuracy evaluation for summarization — Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: A design company uses a foundation model (FM) on Amazon Bedrock to create images for a variety of projects. The company wants control over how detailed or abstract each generated image is. Which model parameter should the company change?
questions.explanation: Generation steps control the number of iterative refinement passes used to create an image. More steps generally yield a more detailed, refined result, while fewer steps can yield a simpler or more abstract result.

questions.questionText: An ecommerce company wants to enhance search recommendations by tailoring results to every user of its ecommerce platform. Which AWS service satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize builds personalized recommendations and can tailor user experiences using customer interaction and item data, making it suitable for customized ecommerce search recommendations.

questions.questionText: A research group wants to test different generative AI models for creating research papers. The group has defined a prompt and needs a way to assess the models’ output. The group wants a team of scientists to perform the output assessments. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use automatic evaluation on Amazon Personalize.
B. Use content moderation on Amazon Rekognition.
C. Use model evaluation on Amazon Bedrock.
D. Use sentiment analysis on Amazon Comprehend.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock model evaluation supports human-based evaluations of generative-model responses. It can use a custom prompt dataset and a work team of employees or subject-matter experts to rate or compare model outputs.
learnMore: Evaluate the performance of Amazon Bedrock resources
Manage a work team for human evaluations of models in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: Which option represents a disadvantage of using generative AI models in production systems?
options: A. Possible high accuracy and reliability
questions.explanation: Generative AI models can hallucinate, producing inaccurate or fabricated information. This creates reliability and safety risks when their output is used in production systems.
learnMore: Detect hallucinations for RAG-based systems (AWS)
Minimize generative AI hallucinations with Automated Reasoning checks (AWS)

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A social media company wants to use a large language model (LLM) to summarize messages. The company has chosen a few LLMs that are available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. The company wants to compare the generated output toxicity of these models. Which strategy gives the company the ability to evaluate the LLMs with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: C. Model evaluation with human workers
D. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)
questions.explanation: Automatic model evaluation uses predefined metrics and tools to systematically assess model outputs for toxicity and other quality measures with minimal human intervention. This approach dramatically reduces operational overhead compared to crowd-sourcing, which requires many reviewers, or manual human review. Reinforcement learning from human feedback requires extensive human labeling, making it far more resource-intensive.
learnMore: Create a model evaluation job using built-in metrics (Amazon Bedrock)
Evaluate the performance of Amazon Bedrock resources

questions.questionText: A company operates a website where users make travel reservations. The company wants an AI solution that helps create consistent hotel branding on the website. The AI solution must generate hotel descriptions for the website in a consistent writing style. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock provides access to foundation models for generative text. A text model can be prompted or customized to produce hotel descriptions in a consistent brand writing style. Amazon Comprehend performs natural-language analysis, Amazon Personalize generates recommendations, and Amazon Rekognition analyzes visual content.
learnMore: Using models with Amazon Bedrock
Customize your model to improve its performance for your use case

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company is testing the security of a foundation model (FM). During testing, the company wants to get around the safety features and make harmful content. Which security technique is this an example of?
options: A. Fuzzing training data to find vulnerabilities
questions.explanation: Jailbreaking is the security technique of bypassing or disabling the safety restrictions and guardrails placed on a foundation model to make it produce harmful, unintended, or malicious content. Testing a model's robustness through jailbreak attempts is a common security evaluation practice. Fuzzing targets training data, DoS attacks target availability, and penetration testing is a broader security assessment approach.
learnMore: Detect prompt attacks with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

questions.questionText: A company uses a foundation model (FM) from Amazon Bedrock for an AI search tool. The company wants to fine-tune the model to be more accurate by using the company's data. Which strategy will successfully fine-tune the model?
options: A. Provide labeled data with the prompt field and the completion field.
B. Prepare the training dataset by creating a .txt file that contains multiple lines in .csv format.
C. Purchase Provisioned Throughput for Amazon Bedrock.
D. Train the model on journals and textbooks.
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning foundation models requires labeled training data structured as prompt-completion pairs, where each prompt represents input and completion represents the desired output. This format allows the model to learn patterns specific to the company's use case. CSV files, provisioned throughput, and training on textbooks do not constitute proper fine-tuning data structure.
learnMore: Prepare data for fine-tuning your models - Amazon Bedrock
Customize a model with fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company uses a foundation model (FM) to generate product descriptions. The model occasionally produces inaccurate information. Which potential generative AI risk does this represent?
questions.explanation: Hallucinations occur when a generative AI model produces false, fabricated, or otherwise inaccurate information that is presented as if it were factual.
learnMore: Contextual grounding check for hallucinations
Minimize hallucinations with Automated Reasoning checks

questions.questionText: A company has implemented a translation tool to help its customer service team address issues from customers worldwide. The company wants to assess the translation tool’s performance. It establishes a parallel data process that compares the tool’s responses with responses from actual humans. Both response sets are generated from the same set of documents. Which strategy should the company use to evaluate the translation tool?
options: A. Use the Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score to estimate the absolute translation quality of the two methods.
B. Use the Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score to estimate the relative translation quality of the two methods.
C. Use the BERTScore to estimate the absolute translation quality of the two methods.
D. Use the BERTScore to estimate the relative translation quality of the two methods.
questions.explanation: BLEU measures the similarity between machine-translated output and high-quality reference translations by comparing matching n-grams. Using the same document corpus and human responses as references enables BLEU scores to compare the translation tool’s quality relative to the human method; BLEU does not provide a reliable absolute measure of translation quality across contexts.
learnMore: The BLEU translation quality metric

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company needs to detect unauthorized API activity for foundation models (FMs) in Amazon Bedrock. Which solution fulfills these requirements?
options: A. Configure AWS CloudTrail to monitor API activity.
B. Use AWS Trusted Advisor to monitor model input and output data.
C. Create Amazon QuickSight dashboards to monitor row-level safety.
D. Monitor user access by using Amazon Personalize.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records Amazon Bedrock API calls as events and includes details such as the requesting identity, source IP address, time, and requested action. These audit records can be monitored and analyzed to identify unauthorized API activity.
learnMore: Monitor Amazon Bedrock API calls using CloudTrail

questions.questionText: Select the appropriate AWS service or tool from the list for each use case. Select each AWS service or tool once, or do not select it.
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth supports human-in-the-loop labeling to produce high-quality ML training data. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provides configurable safety and privacy safeguards for generative AI applications. Amazon SageMaker Clarify detects and measures bias in pre-training data and models.
learnMore: Training data labeling using humans with Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company needs to fine-tune an ML model hosted on Amazon Bedrock. The company plans to use its own sensitive data, which is stored in private databases in a VPC. The data must remain inside the company’s private network. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Restrict access to Amazon Bedrock by using an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) service role.
B. Restrict access to Amazon Bedrock by using an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) resource policy.
C. Use AWS PrivateLink to connect the VPC and Amazon Bedrock.
D. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt the data.
questions.explanation: AWS PrivateLink provides an interface VPC endpoint that privately connects a VPC to Amazon Bedrock, allowing Bedrock API access without an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN, or public IP addresses. IAM policies control permissions and AWS KMS encrypts data, but neither provides the required private network connectivity.

questions.questionText: Which Amazon Bedrock foundation model (FM) can be fine-tuned for comprehension of text, images, and video?
options: B. Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings G1
C. Amazon Titan Text G1 - Express
questions.explanation: Amazon Nova Pro is a fine-tunable multimodal model that accepts text, image, and video inputs, enabling customization for comprehension tasks across all three modalities.
learnMore: Nova Pro - Amazon Bedrock
Customize a model with fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner uses Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management to build a reusable prompt. The prompt must be capable of interacting with external services by calling an external API. Which solution meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: A tools configuration defines the tools a compatible model can use while generating a response, enabling the model to invoke an external API capability. Prompt variables provide value substitution, and stop sequences only determine when generation stops.
learnMore: Create a prompt using Prompt management - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: An animation company needs to provide subtitles for its content. Which AWS service fulfills this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Transcribe automatically converts spoken audio to text and can generate video subtitle files in WebVTT or SubRip formats.
learnMore: Creating video subtitles - Amazon Transcribe

questions.questionText: Which machine learning technique uses training data labeled with the correct output values?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning trains a model on input examples paired with their known correct output values (labels).
learnMore: Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning - AWS

questions.questionText: A company wants to invoke one Amazon Bedrock endpoint and requires Amazon Bedrock to select the most appropriate foundation model (FM) for each request. The company does not want to hardcode a model. Which Amazon Bedrock feature or resource meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock prompt routing provides one serverless endpoint that dynamically routes each request to a suitable foundation model based on its routing criteria and predicted response quality. It eliminates the need for application-side model-selection logic.
learnMore: Understanding intelligent prompt routing in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company’s large language model (LLM) is experiencing hallucinations. How can the company reduce hallucinations?
options: A. Set up Agents for Amazon Bedrock to supervise the model training.
B. Use data pre-processing and remove any data that causes hallucinations.
C. Decrease the temperature inference parameter for the model.
D. Use a foundation model (FM) that is trained to not hallucinate.
questions.explanation: A lower temperature inference setting reduces randomness by favoring higher-probability token choices, producing more deterministic and predictable model responses. This can reduce hallucinated outputs, although it does not eliminate them entirely.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly characterizes Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)?
options: A. A process that uses large amounts of new data to train large language models (LLMs) to improve LLM performance
B. A process by which large language models (LLMs) reference external authoritative knowledge bases to enhance the relevance and accuracy of LLM responses without re-training
C. A process that limits large language models (LLMs) exclusively to their original training data to improve response speed for business applications without re-training
D. A process that focuses on language translation tasks for businesses that operate in multiple countries
questions.explanation: Retrieval Augmented Generation retrieves relevant content from external, authoritative knowledge bases and incorporates it into a model’s response generation. It can improve relevance and factual accuracy without retraining the large language model.
learnMore: What is RAG? (AWS)

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company has deployed an ML model and wants to give external customers secure access to it through the customers’ own applications. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use a custom script in the customers' application for authentication.
B. Store model credentials and share them with the customers directly for authentication.
C. Create a secure API endpoint that customers can use.
D. Embed the model directly into the customers' applications.
questions.explanation: A secure API endpoint exposes the model’s inference capability while keeping the model and its credentials under company control. The endpoint can enforce authentication and authorization for each customer application and protect requests in transit. Amazon API Gateway, for example, supports access-control mechanisms such as JWT authorizers, Lambda authorizers, and IAM authorization for HTTP APIs.
learnMore: Control and manage access to HTTP APIs in API Gateway

questions.questionText: A company wants to enhance a large language model (LLM) for content moderation within 3 months. The company wants the model to moderate content in accordance with the company's values and ethics. The LLM must also be capable of handling emerging trends and new forms of problematic content. Which solution will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Conduct continuous pre-training on a large amount of text-based internet content.
B. Create a high quality dataset of historical moderation decisions.
C. Fine-tune the LLM on a diverse set of general ethical guidelines from various sources.
D. Conduct reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) by using real-time input from skilled moderators.
questions.explanation: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) aligns model behavior with human preferences by using feedback in the reward signal. Real-time feedback from skilled moderators can express the company’s moderation values and continually incorporate newly emerging forms of problematic content.
learnMore: Data lifecycle in generative AI - AWS Prescriptive Guidance
Customize a model with reinforcement fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A documentary filmmaker wants to reach a larger audience. They want to automatically add subtitles and voice-overs in multiple languages to their films. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Use Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Translate to generate subtitles in other languages.
B. Use Amazon Textract and Amazon Translate to generate subtitles in other languages.
C. Use Amazon Polly to generate voice-overs in other languages.
D. Use Amazon Translate to generate voice-overs in other languages.
E. Use Amazon Textract to generate voice-overs in other languages.
questions.explanation: Amazon Transcribe provides speech-to-text and subtitle output for media, while Amazon Translate translates the resulting text into other languages. Amazon Polly converts translated text into lifelike speech, enabling voice-overs in the target languages. Amazon Textract is for extracting text from documents and images, and Amazon Translate is a text-translation service rather than a speech-synthesis service.
learnMore: Creating video subtitles - Amazon Transcribe
What is Amazon Translate?

questions.questionText: A social media company uses an AI-based “Add as Friend” recommendation system. The company wants to make sure its AI models are transparent and explainable. Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?
options: A. Use Amazon Rekognition to analyze user profile pictures to improve model recommendations.
B. Use Amazon SageMaker Clarify to enhance the explainability of model recommendations.
C. Migrate the AI model to Amazon Personalize to improve model recommendations.
D. Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to manually detect model bias.
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Clarify provides managed model-explainability capabilities, including feature attributions that show how input features contributed to individual predictions and overall model behavior. This directly supports transparent, interpretable recommendation outcomes without building a separate explanation system.
learnMore: Model Explainability - Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: A company has fine-tuned a large language model (LLM) to answer questions for a help desk. The company wants to determine if the fine-tuning has enhanced the model's accuracy. Which metric should the company use for the evaluation?
questions.explanation: The F1 score is a balanced metric that combines precision (correctness of answers) and recall (completeness of relevant information retrieval). For a help desk question-answering model, both metrics are important—the model must provide correct answers while retrieving all relevant information. The F1 score harmonizes these concerns, making it ideal for evaluating fine-tuned LLM performance. Precision alone ignores recall, time-to-first-token measures latency, and word error rate is for speech recognition.
learnMore: Use metrics to understand model performance - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: At which stage of the generative AI model lifecycle is the model tested to assess its accuracy?
questions.explanation: The evaluation stage uses tests and metrics to measure a generative AI model’s accuracy and overall performance.
learnMore: Generative AI lifecycle - AWS Well-Architected

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner needs to rapidly deploy and fine-tune foundation models (FMs) for generative AI (GenAI) tasks. The practitioner requires access to pretrained models, solution templates, and example notebooks to speed up development. Which AWS feature or resource fulfills these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart provides pretrained foundation models that can be deployed and fine-tuned, together with solution templates and executable example notebooks that accelerate machine learning and generative AI development.
learnMore: SageMaker JumpStart pretrained models
SageMaker JumpStart Foundation Models

questions.questionText: A financial company trains a generative AI model to predict loan-application outcomes. The training dataset is small and classifies loan applicants as “younger-aged,” “middle-aged,” or “older-aged.” Most people in the dataset are characterized as “middle-aged.” The company removes the age-range feature from the training dataset. Which model behavior is likely to result from this dataset change?
options: A. The model will inaccurately predict outcomes for younger and older age groups.
B. The model will require less training data.
C. The model will predict accurate outcomes for only younger age groups.
D. The model will accurately predict outcomes for all ages.
questions.explanation: A small training set dominated by middle-aged applicants provides comparatively little evidence about outcome patterns for younger- and older-aged applicants. Removing the age-range feature does not correct that imbalance and can prevent the model from learning relevant differences among age groups, making predictions for the underrepresented groups more likely to be inaccurate.
learnMore: Pre-training bias metrics (Amazon SageMaker Clarify)
Class Imbalance (CI) bias metric (Amazon SageMaker Clarify)

questions.questionText: A company has designed an AI-powered agent to answer customer inquiries using product manuals. Which strategy can increase customers’ confidence in the AI-powered agent’s responses?
options: A. Writing the confidence level in the response
B. Including referenced product manual links in the response
C. Designing an agent avatar that looks like a computer
D. Training the agent to respond in the company's language style
questions.explanation: Links to the referenced product manuals give customers source attribution they can review to verify the response. This makes the answer transparent and grounded in authoritative documentation. AWS guidance for knowledge bases notes that generated-response citations let the original data source be referenced and its accuracy checked.

questions.questionText: A company wants to use generative AI to increase developer productivity and software development. The company wants to use Amazon Q Developer. What can Amazon Q Developer do to help the company meet these requirements?
options: A. Create software snippets, reference tracking, and open source license tracking.
B. Run an application without provisioning or managing servers.
C. Enable voice commands for coding and providing natural language search.
D. Convert audio files to text documents by using ML models.
questions.explanation: Amazon Q Developer assists developers by generating code snippets, tracking reference sources for code, and monitoring open-source license compliance. These capabilities directly increase productivity in the software development lifecycle. Serverless computing, voice commands, and audio transcription are AWS services for different purposes and not Q Developer's features.

questions.questionText: A company produces video content and wants to use generative AI to create new creative content while reducing video-production time. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?
options: A. Use the Amazon Titan Image Generator model on Amazon Bedrock to generate intermediate images. Use video editing software to create videos.
B. Use the Amazon Nova Canvas model on Amazon Bedrock to generate intermediate images. Use video editing software to create videos.
C. Use the Amazon Nova Reel model on Amazon Bedrock to generate videos.
D. Use the Amazon Nova Pro model on Amazon Bedrock to generate videos.
questions.explanation: Amazon Nova Reel is Amazon Bedrock’s dedicated video-generation model. It produces videos directly from text prompts or from text and reference-image prompts, eliminating the separate intermediate-image generation and video-editing workflow required by the image-model options.
learnMore: Generating videos with Amazon Nova Reel

questions.questionText: A company is creating an ML model to predict customer churn. Which evaluation metric assesses the model’s performance for a binary classification task such as churn prediction?
options: D. Time used to train the model
questions.explanation: F1 score is a binary-classification metric that balances precision and recall using their harmonic mean. It evaluates how effectively a model distinguishes churn from non-churn predictions.
learnMore: Binary Classification - Amazon Machine Learning

questions.questionText: An online media-streaming company wants to enable its customers to perform natural-language-based image searching and filtering. The company requires a vector database that supports similarity searches and nearest-neighbor queries. Which AWS service fulfills these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service supports vector search, storing embeddings and using k-nearest-neighbor (k-NN) queries to retrieve semantically or visually similar items. Its vector-search capabilities are suitable for image search and similarity-based filtering.
learnMore: Vector search in Amazon OpenSearch Service
k-Nearest Neighbor (k-NN) search in Amazon OpenSearch Service

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company has a team of AI practitioners who build and maintain AI applications in an AWS account. The company must retain records of the actions each AI practitioner performs in the AWS account for audit purposes. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records actions by users, roles, and AWS services as account events, including the identity that performed the action. These event logs provide the audit record of activity in the AWS account.
learnMore: What Is AWS CloudTrail?

questions.questionText: In the context of AI, what does inference refer to?
options: A. The process of creating new AI algorithms
B. The use of a trained model to make predictions or decisions on unseen data
C. The process of combining multiple AI models into one model
D. The method of collecting training data for AI systems
questions.explanation: Inference uses a trained model to process new, previously unseen input and produce a prediction, decision, or response.
learnMore: Google Machine Learning Glossary: Generative AI

questions.questionText: A company is incorporating AI into its employee recruitment and hiring solution. The company wants to reduce bias risks and uphold responsible AI practices while prioritizing fair hiring decisions. Which core dimensions of responsible AI should the company consider? Choose two
questions.explanation: Fairness requires AI systems to avoid unjustified disparities and provide equitable outcomes, which directly addresses bias in hiring. Transparency requires clarity about how the system operates, makes decisions, and its limitations, enabling appropriate scrutiny of AI-supported hiring decisions.
learnMore: What is Responsible AI - Azure Machine Learning

questions.questionText: A company is building a generative AI application that automatically produces product descriptions for an ecommerce website. The product descriptions must be paragraphs of text with a consistent style and tone. The application must create thousands of unique descriptions every day. Which type of generative model meets these requirements?
options: D. A generative adversarial network (GAN) model
questions.explanation: Transformer-based language models are designed for natural-language generation and use attention to preserve contextual relationships throughout a paragraph. They can generate many distinct product descriptions at scale and can be prompted or fine-tuned to maintain a specified style and tone. Microsoft Learn identifies transformers as models used for text generation, whereas GANs and VAEs are commonly used for image generation.
learnMore: Generative AI with Azure Database for PostgreSQL

questions.questionText: A company wants to build a chatbot that responds to questions about human-resources policies. The company uses a large language model (LLM) and has a large digital documentation base. Which technique should the company use to optimize the generated responses?
questions.explanation: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) retrieves the most relevant HR-policy documents for each request and provides them as context to the LLM, grounding responses in the company’s documentation.

questions.questionText: An ecommerce company is building an AI application that categorizes product images and extracts specifications. The application will use a high-quality labeled dataset to customize a foundation model (FM) so that it produces accurate responses. Which ML technique, using Amazon Bedrock, will satisfy these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock supervised fine-tuning trains a foundation model on labeled examples for specific tasks, adjusting the model to produce the desired outputs more accurately. It is appropriate for task-specific image categorization and specification extraction when a high-quality labeled dataset is available.
learnMore: Customize your model to improve its performance for your use case
Customize a model with fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: Choose the correct AI term from the list for each statement. Use each AI term one time.
questions.explanation: Artificial intelligence simulates human-like problem-solving. Machine learning learns patterns from data to make predictions, while deep learning is a machine-learning approach based on multilayer neural networks.

Deep Learning vs Machine Learning - AWS

questions.questionText: A company plans to use its documents as a knowledge base for a large language model (LLM) in a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) solution. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Encrypt each document with encryption keys.
B. Create embeddings from document chunks.
C. Label the document data with metadata.
D. Generate one-hot encoding for each document
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant context through semantic similarity search. Creating embeddings for document chunks produces vector representations that can be compared to a query embedding, allowing the system to retrieve the most relevant chunks for the LLM. Microsoft Learn: How to Use Fabric for Retrieval Augmented Generation
learnMore: How to Use Fabric for Retrieval Augmented Generation

questions.questionText: A company uses supervised learning to train an AI model with a small, labeled dataset tailored to a target task. Which stage of the foundation model (FM) lifecycle does this represent?
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained foundation model to a particular target task by further training it with a smaller labeled, task-specific dataset using supervised learning.
learnMore: Model lifecycle (Amazon Bedrock)
Fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner is building a recommendation system. The practitioner needs to document a business problem, data assumptions, training considerations, and risks of use. The company must adhere to transparency and governance guidelines. Which Amazon SageMaker AI feature meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker AI Model Cards provide a structured, versioned record of a model’s business problem, intended uses and development assumptions, training details, evaluation information, and risk considerations. This documentation supports transparent model reporting and governance throughout the model lifecycle.
learnMore: Model governance to manage permissions and track model performance

questions.questionText: Which AWS service produces business-intelligence reports and automatically creates executive summaries from user-provided data?
questions.explanation: Amazon Q in QuickSight provides generative business-intelligence capabilities in Amazon QuickSight, including generating executive summaries of dashboard insights from the underlying data.
learnMore: Generative BI with Quick Sight
Creating executive summaries

questions.questionText: A company analyzes financial transaction records and classifies them as either personal or business. The company adds these categories to the transaction records. Which data-preparation step is being described?
questions.explanation: Data labeling assigns category or target labels to individual records so they can be used for analysis or supervised machine learning. Marking each transaction as personal or business is therefore data labeling.
learnMore: Data labeling with Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company has deployed a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) application on Amazon Bedrock that collects financial news for distribution in daily newsletters. Users have recently reported politically influenced ideas in the newsletters. Which Amazon Bedrock guardrail can detect and filter this content?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock denied topics are configurable, context-aware policies for subjects that are undesirable in an application’s inputs or model responses. A denied topic for political content can therefore identify and block politically influenced newsletter content.
learnMore: Block denied topics to help remove harmful content - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company is developing a mobile app for people with visual impairments. The app must be able to listen to users' speech and deliver spoken responses. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use a deep learning neural network to perform speech recognition.
B. Build ML models to search for patterns in numeric data.
C. Use generative AI summarization to generate human-like text.
D. Build custom models for image classification and recognition.
questions.explanation: Speech-recognition models, commonly implemented with deep neural networks, process spoken audio and convert it into text or recognized commands. This enables an application to understand what a user says; the resulting response can be delivered through a speech-output capability.
learnMore: What is Amazon Transcribe? (deep-learning ASR)

questions.questionText: A company is rolling out a new AI application that generates content for internal users. Which strategy will make the application’s output more deterministic?
questions.explanation: Lowering the temperature reduces randomness in model sampling, producing more focused and deterministic outputs. Learning rate affects model training, and stop sequences and token limits control where or how long generation ends rather than reducing sampling variability.
learnMore: OpenAI API Reference — Runs

questions.questionText: An ecommerce company wants to build a solution to determine customer sentiments based on written customer reviews of products. Which AWS services meet these requirements? Choose two
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend is a fully managed NLP service that provides built-in sentiment analysis capabilities to classify text as positive, negative, neutral, or mixed—making it directly suitable for analyzing customer reviews. Amazon Bedrock provides access to foundation models that can be configured for advanced sentiment analysis through generative AI, offering an alternative approach. Together, these services form a complete sentiment analysis solution from both traditional NLP and foundation model perspectives.
learnMore: Sentiment – Amazon Comprehend
Introduction – Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company wants to use a large language model (LLM) to produce product descriptions. The company wants to provide the model with example descriptions that follow a particular format. Which prompt-engineering technique will generate descriptions that conform to that format?
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting includes several examples that demonstrate the desired output structure, allowing the model to infer and reproduce the same format in new product descriptions.
learnMore: Few-shot prompt engineering with Amazon Bedrock
Prompt engineering concepts - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company is using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with Amazon Bedrock and Stable Diffusion to generate product images based on text descriptions. The results are often random and lack specific details. The company wants to increase the specificity of the generated images. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Increase the number of generation steps.
B. Use the MASK_IMAGE_BLACK mask source option.
C. Increase the classifier-free guidance (CFG) scale.
questions.explanation: Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) scale is a technique in diffusion models that increases the model's adherence to the text prompt by amplifying the difference between conditional and unconditional predictions. A higher CFG scale makes generated images more closely aligned with the input description, directly reducing randomness and specificity issues. While prompt strength (option D) is sometimes used interchangeably in some contexts, CFG scale is the more precise technical term for Stable Diffusion's mechanism to improve prompt fidelity.
learnMore: Stability AI models - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: An airline company plans to build a conversational AI assistant that answers customer inquiries about flight schedules, booking, and payments. The company wants to use large language models (LLMs) and a knowledge base to build a text-based chatbot interface. Which solution satisfies these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
options: A. Train models on Amazon SageMaker Autopilot.
B. Develop a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) agent by using Amazon Bedrock.
C. Create a Python application by using Amazon Q Developer.
D. Fine-tune models on Amazon SageMaker Jumpstart.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases provides managed retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) capabilities, including document ingestion, retrieval, and prompt augmentation for LLM responses. A Bedrock RAG agent can therefore deliver a knowledge-grounded conversational chatbot with substantially less custom model training or application development.
learnMore: Knowledge bases for Amazon Bedrock
Augment response generation for your agent with knowledge base

questions.questionText: An education company is developing a chatbot for teenagers. The company is training a custom large language model (LLM) and wants the chatbot to use the target audience’s language style, including creative spelling and abbreviated words. Which metric will evaluate the LLM’s performance?
options: C. Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE)
questions.explanation: BERTScore evaluates generated text using contextual embeddings, so it can recognize semantic similarity even when wording differs through creative spelling or shortened words. This makes it more appropriate than exact n-gram overlap metrics such as BLEU or ROUGE for evaluating this language style.
learnMore: Use metrics to understand model performance - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company is developing an ML model to make loan approvals. The company must implement a solution to detect bias in the model. The company must also be able to explain the model's predictions. Which solution will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Clarify is purpose-built to detect bias in ML models and explain model predictions through feature attribution analysis. For loan approval models, it provides fairness metrics to identify disparate impact across demographic groups and explainability tools to show why predictions are made. Data Wrangler (B) prepares data, Model Cards (C) document models, and AI Service Cards (D) describe AWS managed services.
learnMore: Fairness, explainability and bias detection with SageMaker Clarify
Evaluate, explain, and detect bias in models

questions.questionText: A company plans to build a new ML solution. It already has data and needs to understand the ML lifecycle before it builds the solution.
questions.explanation: An ML solution is built by preparing suitable training data, training the model, testing/evaluating its performance, and then deploying the validated model for use.
learnMore: Well-Architected machine learning lifecycle (AWS)

questions.questionText: Which metric measures the runtime efficiency of operating AI models?
options: B. Training time for each epoch
questions.explanation: Average response time (latency) is the primary metric for measuring runtime efficiency of AI models during inference. It reflects how quickly the model processes a request and returns predictions, which is essential for evaluating performance in real-time applications. Customer satisfaction is a business outcome, training time measures training efficiency not runtime, and instance count relates to training data volume.
learnMore: MLPER-03: Define relevant evaluation metrics

questions.questionText: A pharmaceutical company wants to analyze user reviews of new medications and provide a concise overview for each medication. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a time-series forecasting model to analyze the medication reviews by using Amazon Personalize.
B. Create medication review summaries by using Amazon Bedrock large language models (LLMs).
C. Create a classification model that categorizes medications into different groups by using Amazon SageMaker.
D. Create medication review summaries by using Amazon Rekognition.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock large language models are purpose-built for natural language processing tasks including text summarization. They can efficiently analyze and synthesize user reviews to generate concise medication overviews. Amazon Personalize is for recommendation systems, SageMaker classification models require explicit labeled training, and Amazon Rekognition is for image/video analysis—none are optimized for text summarization tasks.
learnMore: What is Amazon Bedrock?
Text summarization for model evaluation in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company is building an application that needs to generate synthetic data that is based on existing data. Which type of model can the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) are specifically designed to generate synthetic data by using two neural networks: a generator that creates synthetic samples mimicking real data, and a discriminator that evaluates quality. This adversarial process produces realistic synthetic data matching the distribution of existing data. XGBoost is a gradient boosting algorithm (not generative), residual neural networks classify images, and WaveNet generates audio sequences—none are designed for synthetic data generation.
learnMore: What is a GAN? – AWS

questions.questionText: A company is building an ML model. The company collected new data and analyzed the data by creating a correlation matrix, calculating statistics, and visualizing the data. Which stage of the ML pipeline is the company currently in?
questions.explanation: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) is the stage where practitioners analyze and visualize data to understand its structure, characteristics, and relationships. Creating correlation matrices, calculating statistics, and visualizing data are hallmark EDA activities that occur early in the ML pipeline to inform subsequent preprocessing and feature engineering decisions.
learnMore: Perform exploratory data analysis (EDA) – Amazon SageMaker AI
Exploratory data analysis with Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler

questions.questionText: What are tokens in the context of generative AI models?
options: A. Tokens are the basic units of input and output that a generative AI model operates on, representing words, subwords, or other linguistic units.
B. Tokens are the mathematical representations of words or concepts used in generative AI models.
C. Tokens are the pre-trained weights of a generative AI model that are fine-tuned for specific tasks.
D. Tokens are the specific prompts or instructions given to a generative AI model to generate output.
questions.explanation: Tokens are the fundamental discrete units of text that generative AI models process during inference and generation—representing words, subwords, or characters depending on the tokenization scheme used by the model.
learnMore: Key terminology (Amazon Bedrock)

questions.questionText: What is the role of vector embeddings in a large language model (LLM)?
options: A. Splitting text into manageable pieces of data
B. Grouping a set of characters to be treated as a single unit
C. Providing the ability to mathematically compare texts
D. Providing the count of every word in the input
questions.explanation: Vector embeddings represent text as numerical vectors that preserve semantic relationships, allowing texts to be compared mathematically for similarity or relatedness.
learnMore: OpenAI API Reference — Embeddings

questions.questionText: A company wants to build an interactive application for children that generates new stories based on classic stories. The company wants to use Amazon Bedrock and needs to ensure that the results and topics are appropriate for children. Which AWS service or feature will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock provide built-in safety mechanisms and content filtering policies that prevent inappropriate topics and ensure generated content adheres to age-appropriate guidelines. For a children's storytelling application, guardrails automatically block harmful, explicit, or unsuitable content before delivery. Rekognition is for image analysis; playgrounds are testing environments; agents are for multi-step workflows.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon SageMaker AI to build AI/ML solutions. The company must use only approved data to train models. The AI/ML solutions must comply with company policy and ethical guidelines. Which solution meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Catalog enables secure discovery and access to approved data and AI assets, with governance-oriented publishing and subscription workflows. It therefore supports restricting model training to approved data while enforcing organizational data and AI governance requirements.
learnMore: What is Amazon SageMaker?

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company is building an editorial-assistant application that uses generative AI. During the pilot phase, usage is low, and application performance is not a concern. The company cannot forecast application usage after the application is fully deployed and wants to minimize application costs. Which solution will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Use GPU-powered Amazon EC2 instances.
B. Use Amazon Bedrock with Provisioned Throughput.
C. Use Amazon Bedrock with On-Demand Throughput.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock On-Demand Throughput is appropriate for an unpredictable, low-volume generative-AI workload because it does not require provisioned compute capacity and charges only for usage. Provisioned Throughput incurs hourly charges for dedicated model capacity and is intended when predictable throughput is needed. AWS documentation
learnMore: Set up inference for a custom model - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company needs to train an ML model to classify images of different types of animals. The company has a large dataset of labeled images and will not label more data. Which type of learning should the company use to train the model?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning is the appropriate choice when training an image classifier with a large dataset of labeled images. In supervised learning, input-output pairs (images and corresponding animal classes) enable the model to learn discriminative patterns. Unsupervised learning (B) requires unlabeled data, reinforcement learning (C) uses reward signals, and active learning (D) requires iterative labeling—all misaligned with having a complete labeled dataset.
learnMore: Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning

questions.questionText: A research company implemented a chatbot by using a foundation model (FM) from Amazon Bedrock. The chatbot searches for answers to questions from a large database of research papers. After multiple prompt engineering attempts, the company notices that the FM is performing poorly because of the complex scientific terms in the research papers. How can the company improve the performance of the chatbot?
options: A. Use few-shot prompting to define how the FM can answer the questions.
B. Use domain adaptation fine-tuning to adapt the FM to complex scientific terms.
C. Change the FM inference parameters.
D. Clean the research paper data to remove complex scientific terms.
questions.explanation: Domain adaptation fine-tuning customizes a foundation model on a specialized dataset (research papers with complex scientific terminology) to improve its understanding and handling of domain-specific language. Since multiple prompt engineering attempts have already been tried without sufficient improvement, fine-tuning is the appropriate next step. Few-shot prompting alone cannot overcome structural limitations; parameter adjustment and data cleaning do not add domain knowledge.
learnMore: Customize models in Amazon Bedrock with fine-tuning and continued pre-training
Supported models for fine-tuning and continued pre-training

questions.questionText: Which term describes the speed at which a pre-trained foundation model (FM) handles requests and produces output?
questions.explanation: Inference latency is the time a model takes to generate a response to a prompt, so it measures request-processing and output-delivery speed.
learnMore: Performance efficiency – Generative AI Lens

questions.questionText: A company has deployed an AI/ML solution to assist customer service agents in responding to frequently asked questions. The questions can change over time. The company wants customer service agents to be able to ask questions and receive automatically generated answers to common customer questions. Which strategy will satisfy these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: B. Train the model by using context data.
C. Pre-train and benchmark the model by using context data.
D. Use Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with prompt engineering techniques.
questions.explanation: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) retrieves relevant, up-to-date content from a knowledge source and adds it to the model prompt when generating an answer. Updating the FAQ content does not require retraining or fine-tuning the model, making it well suited and more cost-effective for changing question-and-answer knowledge.
learnMore: How Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases work
Generative AI options for querying custom documents

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company is developing a custom AI solution in Amazon SageMaker Studio to analyze financial transactions for fraudulent activity in real time. The company must ensure that connectivity from SageMaker Studio to Amazon Bedrock passes through the company’s VPC. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles and policies for SageMaker Studio to access Amazon Bedrock.
B. Configure Amazon Macie to proxy requests from SageMaker Studio to Amazon Bedrock.
C. Configure AWS PrivateLink endpoints for the Amazon Bedrock API endpoints in the VPC that SageMaker Studio is connected to.
D. Configure a new VPC for the Amazon Bedrock usage. Register the VPCs as peers.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock interface VPC endpoints, powered by AWS PrivateLink, provide a private connection from a VPC to the Amazon Bedrock API and runtime endpoints. With private DNS enabled, Amazon Bedrock API calls from the VPC route through that endpoint rather than through public internet connectivity. Use interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) to create a private connection between your VPC and Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company has developed a generative text summarization model by using Amazon Bedrock. The company will use Amazon Bedrock automatic model evaluation capabilities. Which metric should the company use to evaluate the accuracy of the model?
options: A. Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) score
questions.explanation: BERTScore leverages contextual embeddings from pre-trained language models to evaluate semantic similarity between generated summaries and reference text. Unlike surface-level metrics like ROUGE, BERTScore captures deeper meaning and context, making it particularly effective for evaluating generative text summarization quality. It directly aligns with Amazon Bedrock's automatic model evaluation capabilities for text generation tasks. AUC is for classification, F1 score is for classification/retrieval balance, and RWK score is not a standard evaluation metric.
learnMore: Use metrics to understand model performance - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: Which term describes the instructions provided to foundation models (FMs) so that the FMs give a more accurate answer to a question?
questions.explanation: A prompt is the instruction or input given to a foundation model to guide the response it generates.
learnMore: What is a prompt? - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon SageMaker to develop AI models.
questions.explanation: SageMaker Model Registry tracks model packages and their versions through approval and deployment workflows. SageMaker Serverless Inference hosts a model behind an endpoint for on-demand predictions without provisioning or managing servers. SageMaker Clarify is for bias detection and model explainability, not model versioning or inference hosting.
learnMore: Deploy models with Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A financial services company uses AWS to host its generative AI models. The company needs to produce reports demonstrating compliance with international regulations for managing sensitive customer data. Which AWS service fulfills these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact provides on-demand AWS security and compliance documents, including ISO, PCI, and SOC reports, which can be supplied to auditors or regulators as compliance evidence.
learnMore: What is AWS Artifact?

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company deploys a foundation model (FM). The company observes that the FM produces answers to user-submitted questions about politics. The company needs to ensure that the model does not send responses to political questions to users. Which AWS solution meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails can define politics as a denied topic and block detected content in both user queries and model responses, returning blocked messaging instead of the model’s political answer.

Detect and filter harmful content by using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

questions.questionText: A company wants to use an ML model to detect harmful language in the comments section of social-media posts. The company will not use labeled data to train the model. Which strategy should the company use to detect harmful language?
options: B. Use Amazon Comprehend toxicity detection.
C. Use Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithms to train the model.
D. Use Amazon Polly to monitor comments.
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend toxicity detection analyzes text for harmful, offensive, or inappropriate content, including hate speech, harassment, insults, profanity, and threats. It is a managed pre-trained capability, so no labeled training dataset is required.

questions.questionText: Which category of AI model is used to predict numeric values?
questions.explanation: Regression models predict numerical values, typically continuous quantities such as a price, temperature, or sales amount.
learnMore: Regression (Amazon Machine Learning)

questions.questionText: A company wants to build a generative-AI solution that produces product-advertisement content, including sample images and slogans.
questions.explanation: Diffusion models generate images from text prompts. Transformer-based language models generate relevant natural-language content such as slogans. Object-detection models identify and locate objects in an image, enabling validation of the placement of brand elements.

Develop a generative AI application

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company uses a pre-trained open-source model to analyze user sentiment for a recently released product. Which action is the company required to perform according to MLOps best practices?
options: A. Use deep learning to perform hyperparameter tuning.
B. Collect user reviews and label each review as positive or negative.
C. Continuously monitor outputs in production.
D. Perform feature engineering on the input dataset.
questions.explanation: MLOps includes continuously monitoring a model’s production performance and behavior so that degradation, drift, staleness, and other output issues can be detected and addressed.

questions.questionText: A large retail bank wants to develop an ML system to help the risk management team decide on loan allocations for different demographics. What must the bank do to develop an unbiased ML model?
options: A. Reduce the size of the training dataset.
B. Ensure that the ML model predictions are consistent with historical results.
C. Create a different ML model for each demographic group.
D. Measure class imbalance on the training dataset. Adapt the training process accordingly.
questions.explanation: To develop an unbiased ML model for loan allocations, it is critical to measure and address class imbalance in the training dataset and adapt the training process accordingly (e.g., through resampling or weighted loss functions). Class imbalance can cause models to favor majority classes, perpetuating bias. Reducing training data (A) is counterproductive; ensuring consistency with historical results (B) perpetuates past biases; creating separate models per demographic (C) is itself discriminatory.
learnMore: SageMaker Clarify: class imbalance bias metric
Pre-training data bias detection

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of chunking in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)?
options: A. To avoid database storage limitations for large text documents by storing parts or chunks of the text
B. To improve efficiency by avoiding the need to convert large text into vector embeddings
C. To improve the contextual relevancy of results retrieved from the vector index
D. To decrease the cost of storage by storing parts or chunks of the text
questions.explanation: Chunking creates smaller, semantically focused passages that can be embedded and retrieved independently from a vector index. Retrieving only the passages most relevant to a query provides more focused context and improves result relevance.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A financial company uses AI systems to obtain customer credit scores as part of its loan application process. The company plans to expand into a new market in a different geographic area and must ensure it can operate there. Which compliance laws should the company review?
options: A. Local health data protection laws
B. Local payment card data protection laws
questions.explanation: Local algorithm accountability laws can regulate AI-driven credit-scoring and lending decisions, including requirements concerning transparency, bias assessment, automated-decision safeguards, and accountability. These laws are directly relevant when deploying an AI credit-scoring process in a new jurisdiction.

questions.questionText: A financial services company needs to ensure that its generative AI-powered chatbot gives factual responses to meet regulatory-compliance requirements. Which solution prevents the underlying foundation model (FM) from hallucinating?
options: A. Use AWS Config to query compliance metadata by using natural language.
B. Configure Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to evaluate user inputs and model responses.
C. Use Amazon Fraud Detector to detect potentially fraudulent online activities.
D. Use AWS Audit Manager to prepare IT audit and compliance reports.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails evaluates user inputs and model responses. Its contextual grounding checks can detect and filter hallucinated responses that are ungrounded in a provided source or factually inaccurate, supporting factual-response controls for regulated applications.
learnMore: Use contextual grounding check to filter hallucinations in responses
Detect and filter harmful content by using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A social media company wants to use a large language model (LLM) for content moderation. The company wants to evaluate the LLM outputs for bias and potential discrimination against specific groups or individuals. Which data source should the company use to evaluate the LLM outputs with the LEAST administrative effort?
questions.explanation: Benchmark datasets are pre-designed, curated collections specifically created for evaluating AI models on fairness, bias, and discrimination. Using established benchmarks requires the least administrative effort compared to alternatives: user-generated content requires manual labeling, moderation logs require subjective review, and content guidelines are inherently subjective. Benchmarks provide standardized, reproducible evaluation with minimal overhead.
learnMore: Use prompt datasets for model evaluation in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A medical company is customizing a foundation model (FM) for diagnostic purposes. The company needs the model to be transparent and explainable to meet regulatory requirements. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure the security and compliance by using Amazon Inspector.
B. Generate simple metrics, reports, and examples by using Amazon SageMaker Clarify.
C. Encrypt and secure training data by using Amazon Macie.
D. Gather more data. Use Amazon Rekognition to add custom labels to the data.
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Clarify is purpose-built to make machine learning models transparent and explainable by generating metrics, reports, and feature importance analyses. It identifies potential bias in data and model predictions, which is critical for regulatory compliance in healthcare and other sensitive domains. Amazon Inspector performs security scanning, Macie detects sensitive data, and Rekognition is for image recognition—none provide explainability or bias measurement.
learnMore: Evaluate, explain, and detect bias in models – Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: A company needs to customize a base model hosted on Amazon Bedrock.
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning trains a model with labeled examples to improve performance on specific tasks. Continued pre-training extends pre-training with raw, unlabeled documents, enabling the model to acquire domain knowledge and to incorporate additional unlabeled data over time.

Continued pre-training (CPT) - Amazon Nova

questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides foundation models (FMs) to help users build and scale generative AI applications?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock provides secure, managed access to high-performing foundation models from leading AI providers, enabling the development and scaling of generative AI applications.
learnMore: Overview – Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: An education company plans to build a private-tutor application. The application will allow users to enter text or submit an image of a question. It will return a written answer along with an explanation of that written answer. Which model type satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: A multimodal LLM can interpret both textual and image inputs and generate a textual response, including an answer and its explanation. Microsoft Foundry documents vision-enabled chat models as large multimodal models that analyze images and provide text responses.
learnMore: Vision-enabled chat model concepts

questions.questionText: A financial company wants to label all credit-card activity as either possibly fraudulent or non-fraudulent, based on transaction data. Which type of ML model satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Binary classification assigns each transaction to one of two categories, such as possibly fraudulent or non-fraudulent.
learnMore: Binary Classification (Amazon Machine Learning)

questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon Bedrock to deploy a generative AI assistant on its website. The AI assistant supports customers with product recommendations and purchase decisions. The company needs to measure the AI assistant’s direct impact on sales performance. Which metric meets these requirements?
options: A. The conversion rate of customers who purchase products after AI assistant interactions.
B. The number of customer interactions with the AI assistant
C. Sentiment analysis scores from customer feedback after AI assistant interactions
D. Natural language understanding accuracy rates
questions.explanation: The conversion rate of customers who make purchases after interacting with the AI assistant measures the proportion of assistant-engaged customers who complete a sale, directly tying the assistant’s use to sales outcomes.
learnMore: Delivering Business Value through Generative AI - AWS

questions.questionText: A company wants to use a large language model (LLM) to generate concise, feature-specific descriptions for the company’s products. Which prompt engineering technique meets these requirements?
options: A. Create one prompt that covers all products. Edit the responses to make the responses more specific, concise, and tailored to each product.
B. Create prompts for each product category that highlight the key features. Include the desired output format and length for each prompt response.
C. Include a diverse range of product features in each prompt to generate creative and unique descriptions.
D. Provide detailed, product-specific prompts to ensure precise and customized descriptions.
questions.explanation: Creating tailored prompts for each product category that highlight key features and specify desired output format and length provides a systematic, scalable approach to prompt engineering. This technique balances customization with efficiency, ensuring concise and feature-specific descriptions without excessive manual editing. Option A requires post-processing, C introduces noise with irrelevant features, and D scales poorly across a product catalog.
learnMore: Prompt engineering concepts - Amazon Bedrock
Design a prompt - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company is using Amazon SageMaker Studio notebooks to build and train ML models. The company stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs to manage the flow of data from Amazon S3 to SageMaker Studio notebooks. Which solution will meet this requirement?
options: A. Use Amazon Inspector to monitor SageMaker Studio.
B. Use Amazon Macie to monitor SageMaker Studio.
C. Configure SageMaker to use a VPC with an S3 endpoint.
D. Configure SageMaker to use S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
questions.explanation: Configuring SageMaker to use a VPC with an S3 endpoint enables secure, private data transfer between SageMaker Studio notebooks and S3 buckets without routing traffic through the public internet. An S3 VPC endpoint (particularly a gateway endpoint) provides the necessary infrastructure to efficiently manage and govern data flow from S3 to the compute environment. Amazon Inspector and Macie are monitoring/security services, while S3 Glacier is for archival storage.
learnMore: Connect to Amazon SageMaker Studio Through an Interface VPC Endpoint

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company operates an application on servers in an Amazon VPC. The company’s application uses Amazon Bedrock APIs for AI capabilities. The company does not want API calls to traverse the public internet. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Use AWS PrivateLink to establish a private connection between the Amazon VPC and Amazon Bedrock.
B. Sign API requests by using an access key ID and a secret access key that is associated with an IAM principal.
C. Move the application to an on-premises server. Make API calls to the public endpoint of Amazon Bedrock.
D. Encrypt the data in transit from clients to the APIs that have been implemented in the Amazon VPC. Encrypt the data in transit for API calls from the Amazon VPC to Amazon Bedrock.
questions.explanation: An Amazon Bedrock interface VPC endpoint powered by AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity between the VPC and Amazon Bedrock. Bedrock API traffic can use this endpoint without requiring an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN connection, or public IP addresses.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company uses multiple ML models and needs to detect changes in the original quality of its models so it can resolve any issues. Which AWS service or feature satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor continuously monitors machine learning models in production, detects drift or deviations in model-quality metrics such as accuracy, and can alert operators so they can take corrective action.
learnMore: Data and model quality monitoring with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor

questions.questionText: A company has terabytes of data in a database that the company can use for business analysis. The company wants to build an AI-based application that can build a SQL query from input text that employees provide. The employees have minimal experience with technology. Which solution meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Generative pre-trained transformers (GPT) excel at natural language understanding and code generation tasks. A GPT model can be fine-tuned to translate natural language employee queries into structured SQL queries, making database access accessible to non-technical users. Residual neural networks are for image classification, support vector machines are for classification/regression, and WaveNet generates audio—none are suited for natural language to SQL translation.
learnMore: What is GPT AI? – AWS

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner wants an LLM to generate outputs that are more diverse and more creative. How should the AI practitioner modify the inference parameter?
options: B. Decrease the Top K value.
questions.explanation: A higher temperature increases randomness in token selection by making lower-probability tokens more likely to be chosen, which produces more diverse and creative responses.

questions.questionText: A financial services company keeps patterns of fraudulent activity in a database and uses the data to perform investigations. The company wants to use a graph-based ML solution to build an AI tool that supports these investigations. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Neptune is a fully managed graph database service designed for highly connected data and fraud-detection use cases. Neptune ML applies graph neural networks to graph data to identify hidden relationships and patterns that can support fraud investigations.
learnMore: What Is Amazon Neptune?

questions.questionText: A company must perform numerical transformations on a set of images to transpose and rotate them. Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?
options: A. Create a deep neural network by using the images as input.
B. Create an AWS Lambda function to perform the transformations.
C. Use an Amazon Bedrock large language model (LLM) with a high temperature.
D. Use AWS Glue Data Quality to make corrections to each image.
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda can run custom image-transformation code on demand, such as code that transposes and rotates images. It is serverless and automatically manages infrastructure and scaling, minimizing operational overhead for image-processing workloads.
learnMore: Get started with Lambda

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A medical company deployed a disease detection model on Amazon Bedrock. To comply with privacy policies, the company wants to prevent the model from including personal patient information in its responses. The company also wants to receive notification when policy violations occur. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon Macie to scan the model's output for sensitive data and set up alerts for potential violations.
B. Configure AWS CloudTrail to monitor the model's responses and create alerts for any detected personal information.
C. Use Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock to filter content. Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms for notification of policy violations.
D. Implement Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to detect data drift and receive alerts when model quality degrades.
questions.explanation: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock enforce content policies to filter sensitive information (such as PII) from model outputs before users receive responses. Combined with Amazon CloudWatch alarms configured to trigger on policy violations, this provides both preventive filtering and alerting. Amazon Macie scans data in S3, not model outputs; CloudTrail logs API calls but doesn't filter content; Model Monitor detects data drift, not privacy violations.
learnMore: Using Amazon CloudWatch alarms

questions.questionText: A company uses a large collection of web data to create a large language model (LLM). The company randomly initializes the model’s weights. Next, the company trains the model on the data using a language-objective modeling function. Which stage of the model-training process does this scenario represent?
questions.explanation: Pre-training builds a foundation model from scratch by learning general language patterns from a very large, broad dataset. Randomly initialized weights trained with a language-modeling objective describe this initial training stage; fine-tuning instead adapts an existing pre-trained model to a narrower task or domain dataset.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of unsupervised learning?
options: A. A model that groups customers based on their purchase history
B. A model that classifies images as dogs or cats
C. A model that predicts a house’s price based on various features
D. A model that learns to play chess by using trial and error
questions.explanation: Grouping customers according to purchase history is a clustering task that discovers natural patterns in unlabeled data, which is an unsupervised-learning approach.
